item.title: Mapping the Market: Colgate-Palmolive shares look ready to extend rally
item.description: Shares in Colgate-Palmolive have gained more than 13% over the last three weeks or so. That rise could be a sign of building momentum for another leg higher, technical analysis suggests.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Romano
item.content:encoded: Shares in Colgate-Palmolive (CL.N) have gained more than 13% over the last three weeks or so. That rise could be a sign of building momentum for another leg higher, technical analysis suggests. Click here for a detailed technical analysis chart. Technical analysis uses charts of past price moves to map out where a market might go next. Over the years, market watchers have come to recognize that certain chart patterns tend to come before gains. Colgate's chart has formed one of them, known as a bull pennant, because it resembles the object that flies above baseball stadiums. It is called a continuation pattern because it usually forms between two rally phases in a stock. The pattern begins with a sharp climb, which forms its vertical part, known as the flagpole. Eventually the shares pause. Analysts call this resting phase consolidation. It happens when some buyers take profits while other investors position themselves for fresh gains. During consolidation the stock moves little in either direction. Lines connecting its highs and lows converge into a symmetrical triangle that narrows from both sides. The pattern is confirmed when the stock breaks above the triangle's upper line. That is what happened last week, when Colgate shares reached $95.33, highest in about 2-1/2 months, according to LSEG data. After a breakout, analysts estimate potential gains by measuring the height of the flagpole. For Colgate, that points to a target of $106 and possibly as high as $109. On the way up, analysts look for chart levels that could act as support -- which works like a floor for prices -- and resistance, which is a ceiling or cap on gains. They also use tools that measure volatility and momentum to back up their view. Volatility is how much a stock's price swings. Momentum reflects how strongly a stock is moving in one direction. One such tool is Bollinger Bands. These are two lines drawn above and below a moving average of the stock's price. A moving average smooths out price swings by averaging prices over a set period. The bands widen when price swings grow larger. Another is Moving Average Convergence Divergence, or MACD. It compares two moving averages of different lengths to show whether buying pressure is building or fading. A third is the Relative Strength Index, or RSI. It gauges the speed of recent price changes to show whether a stock is gaining or losing strength. All three tools suggest Colgate is gaining upward momentum. Even so, the shares could slow near resistance around $100 on their way higher. If the shares start to retreat, a fall below support in the $88 to $90 area would probably end the rally for now. Colgate-Palmolive did not respond to a request for comment. What the chart shows: Colgate has gained more than 13% in three weeks and broke out of a bull pennant pattern, hitting $95.33 Gains could target $106 and possibly $109, with resistance near $100 along the way A fall below support in the $88 to $90 area would likely end the rally for now (Mapping the Market is a daily column written by Reuters journalists. The commentary is based on a technical analysis of financial charts, which helps assess the likelihood of future price moves but does not guarantee the outcome. The column does not constitute investment advice or trading recommendations. )

item.title: Banco Central paraguayo enfrenta presiones por entidad crediticia con vínculos políticos
item.description: El Banco Central del Paraguay y su presidente han enfrentado crecientes pedidos de renuncia en las últimas semanas, a medida que se intensifica el escrutinio sobre cómo supervisaron un banco digital de rápido crecimiento con vínculos políticos.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Banco Central del Paraguay y su presidente han enfrentado crecientes pedidos de renuncia en las últimas semanas, a medida que se intensifica el escrutinio sobre cómo supervisaron un banco digital de rápido crecimiento con vínculos políticos. Senadores del partido gobernante y de la oposición han instado al presidente, Santiago Peña, a destituir a la cúpula de la banca matriz, en un caso que está poniendo a prueba la reputación que ayudó a Paraguay a convertirse en uno de los destinos emergentes de Sudamérica para el capital extranjero, gran parte del cual proviene de Brasil. Las autoridades intentaron insistentemente las últimas semanas calmar al mercado financiero después de que se conociera que los directores de ueno, un banco de capital mayoritariamente local que administra más de 800 millones de dólares en fondos públicos, estaban bajo un sumario administrativo por una operación de venta de cartera. Ueno pasó de ser una empresa local de tecnología financiera de nicho a convertirse en un banco de tamaño medio, con cerca de 3 millones de clientes, en la línea de plataformas digitales como Monzo y Nubank. "El cambio de las autoridades del Banco Central debe hacerse y lo antes posible. Es necesario cuando hay rumores que estos sean evacuados rápidamente. La gente del BCP perdió credibilidad", afirmó a Reuters el senador oficialista Gustavo Leite. Los detalles de la investigación preliminar figuran en un informe que el Banco Central envió este mes al Senado, que buscaba despejar dudas sobre los préstamos de ueno a empresas vinculadas pero terminó avivando los cuestionamientos de legisladores, el gremio de bancos y otras agrupaciones empresariales. "Hay muchas señales de alerta con relación a esa entidad (...) que el Banco Central no aclara. El sistema financiero está sufriendo un daño tremendo", señaló por su parte el senador opositor Rafael Filizzola, que presentó esta semana otro pedido de informe sobre ueno. La Asociación de Bancos del Paraguay integrada por 14 bancos privados, entre ellos Itaú [RIC:RIC:ITUBK.UL] y GNB [RIC:RIC:GNBI.UL], dijo en un comunicado el fin de semana que las respuestas del Banco Central "son incompletas y dejan dudas" y que la solvencia de una entidad "no puede depender de un trato distinto al que reciben las demás". VÍNCULOS POLÍTICOS El caso es políticamente delicado. El presidente del Banco Central, Carlos Carvallo, trabajó anteriormente en ueno y ocupó el cargo de presidente de la entidad hasta agosto de 2023, confirmó la empresa a Reuters. Peña fue socio comercial del grupo propietario del banco hasta marzo de 2025. Ueno afirmó que el actual mandatario nunca mantuvo relación alguna con el banco en calidad de accionista o inversor. Gran parte de la presión para obtener respuestas provino de senadores del Partido Colorado, al que pertenece Peña, en medio de una disputa política por la candidatura presidencial para las elecciones generales del 2028. En una respuesta escrita a Reuters, el Banco Central describió la situación actual como "política-mediática" y negó que haya un conflicto de intereses ya que Carvallo "se ha inhibido en cada decisión vinculada a Ueno Bank (...) más aún, personalmente optó por retirarse de sala cada vez que se discutía o analizaba cualquier caso vinculado a la entidad". La presidencia paraguaya no respondió a un pedido de comentarios. En declaraciones a medios locales a comienzos de octubre, Peña describió la situación como un "desborde" de una cuestión técnica que se llevó al ámbito político y "ha hecho un daño tremendo a la imagen de todo el país". Ueno confirmó a Reuters que se enfrenta a un procedimiento administrativo preliminar y que el asunto sigue en fase de investigación. La empresa señaló que el procedimiento "no constituye una constatación de irregularidad ni una sanción" y que seguirá "colaborando plenamente" con el Banco Central. El caso de ueno puso bajo el foco la estabilidad en la pequeña economía del país, que ha captado importantes volúmenes de capital extranjero en los últimos dos años después de alcanzar por primera vez el grado de inversión y espera un crecimiento económico de 5% este año, mayor al promedio de la región. Entre enero y agosto, los bancos en Paraguay ganaron unos 680 millones de dólares.

item.title: Musk's political baggage clouds prospects for SpaceX-Tesla deal
item.description: The possible merger may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between President Donald Trump and the Democrats.
item.dc:creator: Cassell Bryan-Low, Hyunjoo Jin
item.content:encoded: A possible merger between Elon Musk's rocket company SpaceX (SPCX.O) and carmaker Tesla (TSLA.O) may face bigger obstacles from politics than from regulation, drawing scrutiny in Beijing and potentially igniting a battle between US President Donald Trump and the Democrats. Musk revived speculation about [USN:L4N4661IU TEXT:"a tie-up"] this week, calling a combination "a good idea" and confirming that committees at both companies were reviewing a potential deal, a step toward what could become the largest merger in history and create a company worth about $3.5 trillion. But a merger would also unite one of the US government's most important aerospace and defense contractors with one of the most China-exposed major American manufacturers — a combination likely to raise questions about national security risks both in Washington and in Beijing. Those concerns are unlikely to derail a deal, analysts said, but they would likely leave the combined company exposed to years of political wrangling and pressure from both sides of the Pacific. Tesla's China operations, they said, could become a source of leverage for Beijing in any future dispute with Washington, while a Democratic takeover of the US House of Representatives in next month's midterm elections could subject the deal to congressional investigations and political maneuvering. Democrats immediately raised concerns about the deal's implications, signaling their intent to turn the merger into a political flashpoint ahead of the November 3 midterms. “If Elon Musk moves forward with the merger of Tesla and SpaceX, the deal would carry real risks that antitrust enforcers across the world would scrutinize," said US Senator Cory Booker, a New Jersey Democrat who sits on both the Judiciary and Foreign Relations committees. He added that he was prepared to conduct oversight of any deal: "When one person controls the infrastructure that governments and militaries depend on, his business decisions become national security decisions, too." Musk could seek to address concerns by limiting how closely the two companies are integrated. The greater threat to the deal may come later, however, if a future administration takes a harder line on the relationship between Tesla and a company increasingly tied to US national security, analysts said. "A merger agreement would involve pledges of limits to the connections between SpaceX and Tesla," said Derek Scissors, a senior fellow at the American Enterprise Institute. "I don't think the Trump administration would enforce these limits. However, the next administration could certainly begin to scrutinize a merged entity. This may be the biggest risk to a deal - that it could get unwound in 2029." EXPOSURE TO CHINA For Beijing, a merger would effectively place Tesla's sprawling Shanghai manufacturing hub under the same corporate umbrella as SpaceX, a company that has become deeply embedded in US military and national security activities through its Pentagon work and through Starlink's role in conflicts, including Ukraine. "A formal merger would make it harder for Chinese authorities to treat Tesla as a purely commercial actor, raising risks for future factory expansions, data approvals, or market access," said Alicia Garcia-Herrero, a senior research fellow at the Brussels-based Bruegel think tank. Tesla's reliance on production from Shanghai already gives China considerable leverage over Musk's business empire. A merger could extend that control to a broader corporate group encompassing strategically important assets such as satellite communications, launch services and military-related technologies. GLOBAL REGULATORY HURDLES The deal would also have to navigate a maze of reviews around the world as competition authorities assess its impact on industries ranging from automobiles and satellite communications to artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Musk's close relationship with Trump would likely dispel concerns about potential US regulatory roadblocks to a transaction, analysts said, while antitrust experts see limited competition concerns because the companies operate largely in separate markets. Outside the United States, however, foreign regulators are likely to scrutinize whether a combined company would gain an unfair advantage by integrating technologies spanning automobiles, artificial intelligence and aerospace. Antitrust experts said authorities in markets with powerful domestic auto industries, such as China and South Korea, could examine whether Tesla's access to SpaceX technologies would give it an advantage that rivals cannot replicate, creating barriers for competitors and potentially undermining domestic manufacturers. Regulators could respond by requiring the company to license key technologies to competitors as part of any approval, said Ioannis Kokkoris, a law professor at Queen Mary University of London. A South Korean antitrust official told Reuters that the merger, if pursued, could require an in-depth review of its potential impact on that country's industries. "Korean antitrust officials will be wary of the merger. They will take the merger very seriously," said Lee Hwang, a law professor at Korea University and former Korea Fair Trade Commission official. "The stakes are very high in Korea because it regards both the automotive and aerospace sectors as strategically important industries."

item.title: Meta has strong chance of getting $25 billion New Mexico penalty slashed on appeal, experts say
item.description: Meta Platforms has a strong basis for arguing that the $25 billion penalty New Mexico secured this week in a case stemming from allegations the firm mishandled user data should be reduced on appeal, legal experts said.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Knauth, Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) has a strong basis for arguing that the [USN:L6N46716L TEXT:"$25 billion penalty"] New Mexico secured this week in a case stemming from allegations the firm mishandled user data should be reduced on appeal, legal experts said. The judgment was one of the largest state verdicts against a company in US history. It came after [USN:L6N46716L TEXT:"a jury found"] Meta misled consumers about who had access to their data in the wake of revelations that Cambridge Analytica, a political consulting firm involved in President Donald Trump 's 2016 presidential campaign, had harvested personal data from millions of Facebook users. New Mexico said state law allowed for a penalty of up to $5,000 for each time someone in the state may have seen an allegedly misleading statement from Meta. Experts said the company would likely argue that Judge Francis Mathew should only have considered people who actually saw the statements. "The most vulnerable basis on appeal is going to be the question about whether a violation is going to count, even in the absence of any proof that a particular person saw one of these misrepresentations or relied on them to their detriment," said Peter Ormerod, a law professor at Villanova University. C.J. Mahoney, Meta's chief legal officer, said the company is confident it will win on appeal. The company is expected to appeal the underlying jury verdict and the penalty. Meta has previously said that it does not sell user data and that New Mexico did not prove any consumer had actually been misled and that a penalty in the billions of dollars would risk violating its constitutional rights to due process and protection from excessive fines. New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez said on Wednesday he expected Meta to appeal the judgment and the state stood ready to defend its legal position. He did not immediately respond to a request for further comment. JURY FOUND 43 MILLION VIOLATIONS New Mexico's attorney general sued Meta in 2021, alleging that the company lied to Facebook users about who had access to their data, how the company handled hate speech and misinformation posted on the platform, and other internal policies. Jurors on September 25 found that 26 of 29 statements made by the company and its leadership on those issues were misleading. Multiplying those statements by their potential audience within New Mexico, the jury said the company had committed more than 43 million violations of the state’s consumer protection laws. The state had 1.4 million active Facebook users and a population of 2.1 million as of 2020. Mathew said in his ruling on Wednesday that a penalty of more than $219 billion would be justified under state law, which allows a $5,000 penalty for each violation, but he reduced the amount. The state had urged Mathew to award the state between $35 billion and $40 billion, while Meta said penalties of no more than $3.45 billion were warranted. Ormerod said that even if the company's appeals in state courts fail, Meta could argue to the US Supreme Court that the penalty violated its rights under the US Constitution to due process and against excessive fines. The size of the penalty on its own does not mean it will be overturned, given the New Mexico law allowing for penalties for each willful violation, said Daryl Lim, a professor at Penn State Dickinson Law. But it seems implausible that Meta was really responsible for so much financial harm, a sign the penalty may be unjust, said Eric Goldman, a professor at Santa Clara University School of Law. "It felt like there was a lot of duplicative counting in the calculations," Goldman said. "How many times can a single person be duped by the same entity?"

item.title: Spotify forecasts fourth-quarter profit above estimates on AI bets
item.description: Spotify forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates on Thursday, as the Swedish music streaming company bets on its AI-powered features to drive user growth in the crucial holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spotify (SPOT.N) forecast fourth-quarter profit above Wall Street estimates on Thursday, as the Swedish music streaming company bets on its AI-powered features to drive user growth in the crucial holiday season. The company expects operating income of €820 million ($920.53 million), compared with analysts' average estimate of €813.4 million, according to data compiled by LSEG. Shares of the company were last up more than 3% in volatile premarket trading. Spotify offers AI-powered features such as its AI DJ, which curates personalized music mixes with spoken commentary, and prompt-based playlists that let users describe a mood or listening preference to generate tailored selections. Investors closely monitor the company's profitability as it invests in AI to improve discovery and engagement on the platform to attract more users and fend off emerging music-generation rivals such as Suno and Udio. In the third quarter, the company reported operating income of €672 million, in line with Visible Alpha-compiled analysts' average estimate of €671.8 million. Spotify reported revenue of €4.97 billion in the quarter, compared with estimates of €4.98 billion, according to LSEG data. "This was a quarter where we did what we said. We've built a strong business that keeps compounding, we invest when we see a path for growth, our costs are moderating, and there is more runway ahead," co-CEO Alex Norstrom said in a statement. Spotify's monthly active users forecast of 818 million for the fourth quarter was marginally below Visible Alpha estimates of 819 million, while its outlook for a 10 million increase in premium subscribers to 316 million was above estimates of 314.7 million. ($1 = 0.8908 euros)

item.title: US Supreme Court rulings reshape midterm election battlefield
item.description: The November 3 midterm elections are quickly approaching after an electoral cycle shaped to an unusual degree by decisions of the US Supreme Court, a development that prompted Justice Elena Kagan to voice alarm this week.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: The November 3 midterm elections are quickly approaching after an electoral cycle shaped to an unusual degree by decisions of the US Supreme Court , a development that prompted Justice Elena Kagan to [USN:L1N46700J TEXT:"voice alarm"] this week. Republicans generally have fared better than Democrats in the spate of recent election-related cases, including in rulings on redrawing congressional districts and rolling back campaign finance restrictions. It remains to be seen, however, whether these [USN:L1N4660I0 TEXT:"legal victories will help"] President Donald Trump 's party in its quest to retain control of Congress in the midterms. Democrats need a net gain of four seats each in the House of Representatives and Senate to overcome narrow Republican majorities in those chambers. Ceding control of either chamber to the Democrats would endanger Trump's legislative agenda and open the door to Democratic-led congressional investigations targeting the president. Several Supreme Court rulings last year and this year have helped Republicans, on balance, make the national House map more favorable to their party in the election, though polls indicate Democrats still are in a strong position to secure a majority. The court has a 6-3 conservative majority. In a pair of landmark rulings powered by the conservative justices, the court in April gutted a key provision of [USN:S0N3YR00L TEXT:"the Voting Rights Act"], the 1965 law intended to prevent racial discrimination in voting, and in June threw out longstanding [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"campaign finance limits"] — decisions that have boosted Republicans. But when the court issued a ruling last month rebuffing a Trump-backed effort to [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"restrict mail voting"] — a mode of casting a ballot used more often by Democratic voters — only the court's two most conservative justices, Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito, publicly dissented. Republicans seem to have gained a net benefit from the court's recent election-related rulings, according to law professor Ilya Somin of George Mason University in Virginia, who said some of the key decisions "reflect longstanding conservative jurisprudential priorities." Somin also noted the volume of litigation this cycle, saying, "It strikes me there are a lot more Supreme Court election-related cases than usual, especially in a midterm election." REDISTRICTING ARMS RACE The court's decision that further undercut the Voting Rights Act made it harder for minorities to challenge electoral maps as racially discriminatory. Several Republican-led Southern states responded by rushing to dismantle House districts with sizable Black populations in time for the midterms. Black voters tend to support Democratic candidates. Other Supreme Court rulings allowed starkly partisan voting maps for the midterms, fueling an unprecedented redistricting arms race between Republicans and Democrats. This battle was initiated last year when Trump urged Republican-led states to rip up existing congressional maps and draw new ones more likely to help the party pick up House seats in the midterms. Texas was the first to do so, and the Supreme Court [USN:S0N3VN017 TEXT:"allowed the new map"]. Redistricting traditionally has been carried out by state legislatures at the start of each new decade to reflect population shifts measured by the US Census, not midway through the decade as numerous states have done recently. Kagan, one of the court's three liberal justices, lamented a 2019 [USN:L1N3Z50PN TEXT:"decision"] powered by the conservative justices that helped supercharge this political practice — called gerrymandering — that polling shows most Americans oppose. That ruling, authored by conservative Chief Justice John Roberts, declared that federal courts have [USN:KCN1TS2VP TEXT:"no authority"] to curb gerrymandering done for partisan gain. Kagan [USN:L1N46700J TEXT:"accused"] the court's conservatives of having enabled increased political polarization by not reining in partisan gerrymandering, which involves states redrawing the boundaries of electoral districts based on the partisan leanings of voters to boost a political party's candidates. "It is making what I think is unfortunately a too-polarized country even more so," Kagan told an audience at Catholic University's law school in Washington, expressing concern over implications for American democracy. CAMPAIGN FINANCE The Supreme Court handed Republicans a set of wins on the issue of campaign finance this year. In June, it struck down federal caps on [USN:L1N4310Y4 TEXT:"spending by political parties"] in coordination with candidates in a challenge brought by Trump's vice president, JD Vance, and others. Since then, Republican committees have greatly exceeded these former limits, with their Democratic counterparts doing so to a lesser extent. The court further bolstered coordinated spending this month by allowing a Trump administration policy giving political parties, and not just candidates, access to [USN:S0N45602X TEXT:"discounted TV and radio"] advertising rates. The record for Trump and his political allies has not been perfect at the court, however. The justices last month [USN:S0N43100X TEXT:"barred Missouri"] from using its redrawn pro-Republican congressional map. And while the court permitted Texas to implement its pro-Republican congressional map, it subsequently allowed California's [USN:S0N3WN09U TEXT:"pro-Democratic map"]. Additionally, the court declined last month to let the US Postal Service enforce a rule [USN:S0N431004 TEXT:"targeting mail-in ballots"], following a June decision by the justices endorsing [USN:S0N40Z03J TEXT:"grace periods for mail voting"], over Republican objections. All told, however, the court's election-related rulings so far this cycle have favored the election priorities of Trump and his party, reflecting a broader pattern, according to University of Illinois Chicago law professor Steve Schwinn. "Court rulings this year and over the last decade have decidedly tilted the political playing field in favor of Republicans," Schwinn said. MORE LITIGATION POSSIBLE Trump's history of challenging unfavorable electoral outcomes, including his false claims of widespread voting fraud in the 2020 election he lost to Democrat Joe Biden, suggests the court may be drawn into more electoral disputes after the midterms. State election officials across the country already are bracing for potential federal interference in the voting. The Supreme Court turned away cases in which Trump and his allies challenged the 2020 election outcome. But it subsequently embraced his request for [USN:L1N3IQ192 TEXT:"criminal immunity"] after Trump was indicted on federal charges over his efforts to undo his loss to Biden. "I think additional election litigation is quite likely," George Mason's Somin said. "Whether any of it reaches the Supreme Court is much harder to predict. The court, of course, has broad discretion over which cases it decides to take."

item.title: Investors see risk from US midterms to AI trade as data center backlash builds
item.description: Public opposition to data centers may jolt the AI trade as the US midterm elections approach, with a strong Democratic showing potentially hampering the buildout that has lifted stocks.
item.dc:creator: Lewis Krauskopf
item.content:encoded: Public opposition to data centers may jolt the AI trade as the US midterm elections approach, with a strong Democratic showing potentially hampering the buildout that has lifted stocks. AI has driven the US stock bull market that just marked its [USN:L6N45R12W TEXT:"fourth anniversary"], as companies such as Alphabet (GOOGL.O) and Amazon (AMZN.O) pour money into building data centers. AI's importance to the market makes investors highly sensitive to obstacles that could slow the development pace, with spending on data centers and other AI infrastructure expected to top $1 trillion next year, [USN:L6N45K12P TEXT:"boosting corporate profits"]. Public backlash is one of those obstacles. As the massive data centers proliferate, many Americans are concerned about the strain on the environment and impact on energy costs, as well as about the technology itself. "This is and has become a very tangible issue," said Christopher Gannatti, US chief investment officer at WisdomTree. Since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, he said, "the key signal for the market has been how much money are these five or six huge companies spending" on data centers. Investors have banked on an optimistic outlook for AI expansion, and any question about its rapid growth continuing causes sharp market moves. Several segments of the AI sector have stumbled in recent weeks as debt concerns centered on [USN:L4N461208 TEXT:"cloud company CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) . Democratic victories in both chambers in the November 3 elections, which would wrest control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican Party, pose the greatest AI-related threats of the potential midterm outcomes, market watchers say. A Democratic sweep of the Senate and House of Representatives is the most likely outcome, according to trading on prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket. Analysts are dubious about prospects for national legislation that would significantly stall data center construction. However, they say Democratic leadership of the House and Senate would likely mean more hearings and investigations related to AI and the data center buildout. Investors are also focused on state and local races where data centers have become pivotal issues and where authorities also hold sway over the pace of development. DEMOCRATIC CONGRESS COULD INCREASE AI SCRUTINY AI is not purely a partisan issue, as Republican voters also express concerns about data centers, but opposition appears stronger among Democrats. A Reuters/Ipsos poll released this month showed 69% of Democratic registered voters back limits on building data centers, compared with 43% of Republicans. Even with a Democratic sweep, analysts doubt a bill that significantly impedes data center expansion would become law. Trump — who has been supportive of AI — would likely block such legislation, said Matt Gertken, chief geopolitical strategist at BCA Research. "The bill that is going to pass, and the bill that Trump is willing to sign, will be an AI regulation bill, but it probably won't be slamming the brakes on capex and construction," Gertken said. [USN:FWN4661WE TEXT:"Trump said on Wednesday"] that companies building data centers should pay a "dividend" to communities if they want to make them popular. Some in Congress, even on the Democratic side, might also be reluctant to enact legislation that undermines data center progress, due to its importance for economic growth and because of fears of losing competitive ground to China. Still, if they control Congress, the Democrats are expected to apply more scrutiny to AI, including data centers, which could raise market volatility. "There will be congressional hearings. There will be investigations," said Brian Gardner, chief Washington policy strategist at investment bank Stifel. "You never know where that stuff leads, and there can be negative headlines." LOCAL RACES IN FOCUS FOR DATA CENTER OVERSIGHT The oversight that state and local authorities have over data centers also means investors will be unusually focused on specific elections next month. Investors are watching at least a half dozen states such as Texas for which party wins control of the governor's seat or the legislature, while also following specific House and Senate elections and even votes for positions such as utility commissioner. "Data centers are a real political issue, a really salient one in these state and local races," said Maxwell Shulman, a policy research analyst at Beacon Policy Advisors in Washington. "And depending on which party takes control, there really could be implications for the regulations and the restrictions that data centers might have to face going forward." Strategists at investment bank Morgan Stanley are monitoring the elections for governor in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Nevada, Wisconsin and Michigan. "Because it is so disproportionate, the states where that investment is going really do have to be a focus for investors," Shulman said. Policy uncertainty around data centers is unlikely to "derail" the AI investment theme, said Kevin Shea, senior equity analyst at BNY Wealth. "But what it can do is disrupt the timing and the cost," Shea said.

item.title: Saudi Aramco tells staff to evacuate Dhahran headquarters, sources say
item.description: Oil giant Saudi Aramco has instructed staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oil giant Saudi Aramco (2223.SE) has instructed staff to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, six people with knowledge of the matter said on Thursday. Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The move marked the first time Aramco had asked staff to evacuate its headquarters since the start of the Iran war . Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis caused [USN:L1N46710X TEXT:"extensive damage"] to the company's headquarters earlier this month when they struck the building, with fire spreading across several floors. The facility hosts an operations centre, which helps the world's largest oil company oversee onshore and offshore oil rigs, refineries, export terminals and thousands of kilometres of pipelines. Separately, two people were killed on Wednesday after Saudi air defences intercepted a drone that was attempting to hit a facility at Aramco's Shaybah oilfield. Saudi Arabia has responded to Houthi attacks with a wave of strikes on missile launcher sites, vowing to protect the kingdom, and says it has intercepted many ballistic missiles fired by the group.

item.title: India's Jindal Stainless beats quarterly profit view on strong exports
item.description: India's Jindal Stainless reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Jindal Stainless (JIST.NS) reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports. Here are some key details: Consolidated net profit for India's biggest stainless-steel producer rose to 8.98 billion rupees ($94.7 million) in the quarter ended September 30 from 8.08 billion rupees a year ago Analysts, on average, had expected a profit of 8.36 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG Higher volumes and resilient stainless steel demand were expected to boost second-quarter earnings, according to analysts at ICICI Securities Sales volume rose 2.5% year-on-year to 664,378 tons, led by a 36% jump in exports Domestic sales comprised 89% of total sales, down from 91% a year ago, while exports were 11% of total sales during the quarter Revenue rose 18.2% to 128.74 billion rupees; EBITDA grew 3.2% year-on-year to 14.33 billion rupees The quarter marked a resilient recovery following the operational disruptions in the previous three months, which had been impacted by the geopolitical situation and industrial gas availability constraints - Jindal Stainless The company also flagged increased import pressure, especially from China "The first four months of FY27 alone account for about 63% of the entire previous year's imports from China," the stainless steel maker said Jindal Stainless operates 16 stainless-steel facilities across India, Spain and Indonesia, with a network spanning 12 countries ($1 = 94.8800 Indian rupees)

item.title: Lab testing LBO offers murky result for both sides
item.description: EQT will buy Qiagen for $12 bln, whose kits trace diseases and help police solve crimes. It’s barely more than an offer shareholders rejected back in 2020. Yet the Swedish buyer will need to grow beyond current forecasts and crank up margins to get a decent return.
item.dc:creator: Aimee Donnellan
item.content:encoded: EQT will buy Qiagen for $12 bln, whose kits trace diseases and help police solve crimes. It’s barely more than an offer shareholders rejected back in 2020. Yet the Swedish buyer will need to grow beyond current forecasts and crank up margins to get a decent return. Full view will be published shortly. Follow Aimee Donnellan on LinkedIn . CONTEXT NEWS Sweden's EQT will buy molecular testing company Qiagen for about €9.6 billion ($10.78 billion), the companies said on October 21. Buyout firm EQT offered €46.50 ($52.22) a share for Qiagen, representing an 8.6% premium to its last close. Affiliates of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board are also participating in the offer. The deal, which values Qiagen at about $12.1 billion including about $1.1 billion in net debt, is expected to close in mid-2027. EQT has secured equity and debt financing to fund the offer. Qiagen said it was suspending its full-year 2026 outlook pending the deal. It reported preliminary third-quarter net sales of $548 million and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $0.65. Qiagen shares were trading at €45.12 ($50.70) by 0833 GMT on October 22.

item.title: Southern Italy truckers ease protests as government lines up aid
item.description: Truck drivers' protests that have seriously affected fuel and food supplies in southern Italy were easing on Thursday as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government was lining up aid and taking a harder line against roadblocks.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Piscioneri, Alvise Armellini
item.content:encoded: Truck drivers' protests that have seriously affected [USN:L8N467269 TEXT:"fuel and food supplies"] in southern Italy were easing on Thursday as Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's government was lining up aid and taking a harder line against roadblocks. Since last week, hauliers have been blocking roads and motorways to protest against high fuel prices, but their representatives said roadblocks would be lifted in Sicily following talks with the government. Truck drivers in Calabria also suspended their protest, while Vincenzo Parisi, speaking for hauliers from the Campania region around Naples, told RAI public radio he hoped roadblocks could be lifted in the area later on Thursday. SEVERE DISRUPTION, BUT NO TOILET PAPER SHORTAGES The protests have caused "severe disruption" in Campania, affecting supplies to supermarkets, petrol stations and even hospitals, Deputy Infrastructure Minister Edoardo Rixi told RAI radio. However, Meloni's office dismissed as "ridiculous" a front-page report by opposition newspaper Il Fatto Quotidiano suggesting that government headquarters in Rome were running out of toilet paper due to the truckers' blockades. In Naples, fuel shortages were making it harder for doctors to reach hospitals and clinics and for ambulances to respond to emergencies, the head of the local order of physicians and dentists said. "We understand the truck drivers' concerns, but we are calling for a responsible protest. Fuel supplies for ambulances must be guaranteed and healthcare workers must be able to get to work," Bruno Zuccarelli said. MELONI TO CHAIR MEETING ON APPROVING AID Antonio Ferraioli, chairman and chief executive of tomato sauce and pasta producer La Doria, told la Repubblica daily that the company had stopped production in seven plants in southern Italy and placed half of its workforce on forced leave. "If the protest continues, products from southern Italy will disappear from supermarket shelves across the country and will be replaced by imports or products from other parts of Italy," he said. Meloni was due to chair a cabinet meeting in Rome to approve a decree bringing together aid measures for truck drivers and farmers, including financial compensation measures for high diesel costs. The government also said it was working to ensure the distribution of essential goods, including food and medicines, offering police escorts to trucks seeking to go past roadblocks.

item.title: Índice das principais empresas da China confirma mercado em baixa; setor de IA tem forte queda
item.description: O índice das principais ações da China despencou para a menor cotação em 15 meses e confirmou um mercado em baixa nesta quinta-feira, à medida que as ações do setor de IA caíram devido a temores de que o crescimento e as valorizações fossem insustentáveis.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O índice das principais ações da China despencou para a menor cotação em 15 meses e confirmou um mercado em baixa nesta quinta-feira, à medida que as ações do setor de IA caíram devido a temores de que o crescimento e as valorizações fossem insustentáveis. O Índice CSI300 (.CSI300) caiu 1,8%, fechando em 4.036,30, seu nível mais baixo desde julho de 2025. Ele está agora 20,2% abaixo de sua última alta de fechamento, registrada em 22 de junho, ultrapassando o limiar de 20% que normalmente define um mercado em baixa. O Índice Composto de Xangai (.SSEC) fechou com queda de 1,5%, também seu nível mais baixo em mais de um ano. Com base nos níveis de fechamento, o índice CSI300 nunca superou a alta registrada em 2007, e o ímpeto que levou o mercado a uma alta de cinco anos em junho sofreu uma reversão acentuada desde então. "O mercado está em baixa", disse Hao Hong, sócio-gerente e diretor de investimentos da Lotus Asset Management, em Hong Kong. Uma onda generalizada de vendas entre as principais empresas de tecnologia em toda a Ásia, aliada a expectativas moderadas de estímulos e à falta de novos catalisadores, desencadeou uma forte queda na China. Apenas os subíndices de bens de consumo básico (.CSI000912) e de serviços públicos (.CSI000917) conseguiram registrar ganhos modestos. O Índice CSI de chips (.CSI931865) caiu 3,6% e o Índice CSI de IA (.CSI930713) registrou queda de 3,3%. O Índice Composto ChiNext (.CNT) , da bolsa para startups, despencou 4,4%, atingindo seu nível mais baixo desde julho de 2025. O humor do mercado também foi prejudicado pela decepção com as medidas de estímulo fragmentadas de Pequim, segundo operadores e analistas, enquanto o crescimento econômico no terceiro trimestre, acima do esperado, reduziu ainda mais as expectativas de apoio adicional por parte das autoridades. O crescimento econômico da China saiu de níveis mínimos de três anos, já que as exportações compensaram a cautela dos consumidores em gastar, mesmo com a crescente dependência de fatores externos aprofundando os desequilíbrios estruturais. . Em TÓQUIO, o índice Nikkei (.N225) caiu 2,67%, a 62.907,84 pontos. . Em HONG KONG, o índice HANG SENG (.HSI) caiu 3,03%, a 22.934 pontos. . Em XANGAI, o índice SSEC (.SSEC) perdeu 1,48%, a 3.658 pontos. . O índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em XANGAI e SHENZHEN, retrocedeu 1,84%, a 4.036 pontos. . Em SEUL, o índice KOSPI (.KS11) teve desvalorização de 3,52%, a 5.533 pontos. . Em TAIWAN, o índice TAIEX (.TWII) registrou baixa de 1,81%, a 46.041 pontos. . Em CINGAPURA, o índice STRAITS TIMES (.STI) desvalorizou-se 0,57%, a 5.406 pontos. . Em SYDNEY o índice S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) recuou 0,43%, a 8.793 pontos. (Reportagem da Redação de Xangai e de Hong Kong)

item.title: Pound edges higher, outperforming as investor nerves rattle euro zone markets
item.description: The pound edged up on Thursday, as outflows from euro zone assets saw UK stocks, bonds and the currency outperform other markets in the region.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Cooper
item.content:encoded: The pound edged up on Thursday, as outflows from euro zone assets saw UK stocks, bonds and the currency outperform other markets in the region. Expectations that the Bank of England will raise interest rates next month are also supporting the pound, following higher than expected UK inflation [USN:L8N46708O TEXT:"data"] this week. Sterling was up 0.1% on the day at $1.34, making it one of the stronger performers, aside from the safe-haven Japanese yen and Swiss franc . Money markets show traders expect the Bank of England to deliver at least three quarter-point rate hikes by April, with the first one priced in for the November 5 policy meeting, compared with roughly two hikes by the European Central Bank, thereby widening the interest-rate differential that fuels carry trades. These are lucrative rate-plays that involve borrowing a lower-yielding currency, in this case, the euro, to sell it and fund investment in a higher-yielding currency like the pound. Investor concern about high oil prices, the cost of the AI buildout and the ability of developed-market governments to bring down their huge debt loads rattled riskier assets, particularly in Europe, where French bond yields rose to new 24-year highs and euro zone stocks fell sharply. UK gilt yields were flat on the day , against steep rises in yields on French, Italian and Belgian debt, while the FTSE 100 (.FTSE) fell 0.6% but outperformed the STOXX 600 (.STOXX) , which was down 1%. Over the course of the last month, the pound has been the best-performing major currency against the US dollar, up 0.3%, while the euro is the worst-performing, with a loss of 2%. The euro is heading for a fourth straight week of declines against the pound , having lost another 0.5% so far this week, which brings its decline for the year to 1.8%. If sustained, this would be the euro's largest monthly drop against the pound since May 2023, when it fell 2%. "It looks like there is both independent sterling strength and independent euro weakness at play in euro/sterling. Earlier this summer, we had felt that sterling gains would not last. But now greater market confidence in a Bank of England tightening cycle – we look for 25-bp hikes in February and November – makes sterling a high-carry European currency," ING strategist Chris Turner said. The concern building over the ability of the French government to tackle its finances is also taking its toll on the euro, which traders are betting will fall further against the pound. The options market shows traders are at their most negative over the prospects of the euro against the pound since mid-2024 , according to LSEG data. UK finance minister John Healey delivers his first budget on [USN:L8N46716U TEXT:"October 28"], which major investors expect to pass without rattling markets unduly.

item.title: Manchester City take perfect record to Villa amid off-field turmoil
item.description: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their guilty verdict on financial-rule charges.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester City will try to preserve the Premier League's only perfect record at Aston Villa this weekend while dealing with mounting injuries and major off-field distractions following their [USN:L6N45L10G TEXT:"guilty verdict"] on financial-rule charges. Enzo Maresca's City have won all seven league matches to sit three points clear of champions Arsenal, but an independent commission's finding that the club were guilty of 114 financial breaches has cast a shadow over their blistering start. City have denied any wrongdoing and appealed, with sanctions yet to be decided. Their immediate task is maintaining their flawless run at Villa Park on Saturday despite a growing injury list. Forward [USN:L6N4650QO TEXT:"Antoine Semenyo"] is set for a lengthy spell out with a knee injury, while wing back Nico O'Reilly and midfielders Mateo Kovacic and Matheus Nunes are doubts. League-leading scorer Erling Haaland was rested for Tuesday's [USN:L6N4661C4 TEXT:"5-1"] Champions League thrashing of AEK Athens because of a knock but is expected to be available against Villa. Arsenal, City's closest challengers on 18 points, host Everton on Saturday, although they have fitness concerns after [USN:L1N46802Z TEXT:"Bukayo Saka"] limped off in the 10th minute of Wednesday's [USN:L6N46717X TEXT:"2-2"] Champions League draw at Bayern Munich with a quadriceps injury. "He doesn't look good at all, but we'll have to wait and see," Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said. Fourth-placed Chelsea host London rivals Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on Saturday after back-to-back league victories over Bournemouth and Everton. Spurs finally earned their first league victory of the season with Monday's [USN:L6N4651AC TEXT:"3-1"] home win over Coventry City after a miserable start that has left them 16th with six points from seven games. Chelsea have 13 points. Liverpool face one of the tougher challenges of the weekend when they welcome high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion to Anfield on Sunday. Brighton's superb start has them third with five wins and a draw from seven matches, two places and four points above Liverpool, while their goal difference of plus 18 is the league's best. Liverpool, though, have uncovered another attacking weapon in 18-year-old [USN:L8N4662MN TEXT:"Rio Ngumoha"], who produced a dazzling performance in their 4-3 Champions League comeback win over Villarreal on Tuesday. Ngumoha created two goals and became the youngest Liverpool player to register a Champions League assist, earning a standing ovation from the Anfield crowd. "That's the good thing with Rio he is still 18, he is not the full package, he can add things fortunately for us. Hopefully he can continue in the same way," Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said. "But I'm happy because attitude-wise I think he's in a great place." Liverpool's injury problems complicate the task, with the versatile Dominik Szoboszlai, wing back Jeremie Frimpong, right back Conor Bradley and striker Hugo Ekitike among those sidelined. At Old Trafford, Manchester United desperately need a victory over Bournemouth to breathe life into a season that has gone awry. Michael Carrick's team are 13th with one victory and seven points from their opening seven matches and are coming off a shambolic [USN:L6N4671CM TEXT:"4-1"] Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday. "I have to apologise to the supporters," Carrick said after the latest setback in Italy. "I care about this football club as much as anyone, if not more. "For us to play in that way, it's not acceptable. That bit of intensity, that aggression, that real willingness to give everything tonight was totally the opposite of the performance. It was tough to watch." Complicating matters, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Luke Shaw, Benjamin Sesko, Patrick Dorgu and Lisandro Martinez are among those with injury or fitness concerns, while midfielder Manuel Ugarte has a long-term knee injury. Carrick's United were held 1-1 at home by Tottenham and away to Leeds United in their last two league outings and now face a Bournemouth side who sit one point below them. For Manchester City, the challenge is almost the reverse. While their rivals search for momentum or try to keep pace, they head to Villa attempting to ensure the legal fight surrounding the club does not interrupt a perfect start on the pitch.

item.title: Turkey says it is waiting for sale contract from Qatar for Eurofighter Typhoon jet procurement
item.description: Turkey is waiting for Qatar to send it a sale contract and a draft training programme as part of its deal with Britain to procure Eurofighter Typhoon jets, the Turkish Defence Ministry said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey is waiting for Qatar to send it a sale contract and a draft training programme as part of its deal with Britain to procure Eurofighter Typhoon jets, the Turkish Defence Ministry said on Thursday. NATO allies Turkey and Britain [USN:L1N3W80J0 TEXT:"signed the deal"] for 20 jets last year, in a move aimed at deepening bilateral ties and bolstering Turkish air defences. Ankara has said it was also seeking 24 more jets from Qatar and Oman, though there has been little progress on that procurement. Under the deal with Britain, Qatar and Oman can supply Turkey with some of its own Typhoons, though that requires a separate sales contract. At its weekly press briefing, the ministry said that [USN:L8N3WB0U6 TEXT:"talks on the procurement"] were continuing and that Turkish and Qatari delegations discussed technical and logistical matters in August and September. These included the scope of jets and ammunition to be procured, training for pilots and maintenance teams. "It is expected for Qatar to prepare the draft training programme and the sales contract to be sent to our country," it said. Turkey signed [USN:L6N4670S7 TEXT:"an accord"] with Qatar, Pakistan and Indonesia on Wednesday to boost defence cooperation and strengthen defensive capabilities, including through joint development and production. The ministry added that its defence budget was [USN:L8N4671F9 TEXT:"increased for 2027"] due to ongoing domestic defence industry projects for air defences and platforms, Turkey's indigenous KAAN fighter jet programme, drone development and shipbuilding.

item.title: La prima de riesgo francesa marca un nuevo máximo de 15 años ante inquietudes fiscales y protestas
item.description: El diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos del Estado francés a 10 años y los bonos alemanes, considerados activos refugio, alcanzaba el jueves un nuevo máximo de 15 años, mientras las dudas sobre la capacidad del país para sanear sus deterioradas finanzas públicas y las continuas protestas callejeras seguían lastrando la confianza de los inversores.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo
item.content:encoded: El diferencial de rendimiento entre los bonos del Estado francés a 10 años y los bonos alemanes, considerados activos refugio, alcanzaba el jueves un nuevo máximo de 15 años, mientras las dudas sobre la capacidad del país para sanear sus deterioradas finanzas públicas y las continuas protestas callejeras seguían lastrando la confianza de los inversores. Los ministros franceses han prometido reforzar considerablemente el dispositivo de seguridad durante las nuevas protestas previstas para este sábado, con un despliegue de militares junto con efectivos policiales adicionales. El rendimiento del bono francés de referencia a 10 años subía 6 puntos básicos, hasta el 5,0601%, su nivel más alto desde julio de 2002. Esto elevaba la prima de riesgo francesa frente a los bonos alemanes hasta los 160,90 puntos básicos —su mayor nivel desde noviembre de 2011, durante la crisis de deuda de la zona euro—, lo que reflejaba la inquietud de los inversores por las actuales perspectivas fiscales de Francia. Los diferenciales de rendimiento frente a los bonos alemanes se ampliaban en toda la zona euro. El de Bélgica alcanzaba los 104,89 puntos básicos, su máximo desde 2013, mientras que el de Italia subía 4,5 puntos básicos, hasta los 116,90; el de España se ampliaba 3 puntos básicos, hasta los 66,50; y el de Grecia aumentaba 5,5 puntos básicos, hasta los 99,50. La incertidumbre política ante las elecciones del próximo año en Francia y las dificultades de París para aprobar un presupuesto han lastrado aún más la confianza del mercado. "Existe un consenso en que Europa está hoy mejor preparada para afrontar las crisis y en que las instituciones europeas son más fuertes que hace 15 años, lo que debería facilitar la articulación de una respuesta europea", dijo Giada Giani, economista de Citi, al referirse a las diferencias entre la Francia actual y los países de la periferia europea a principios de la década de 2010. "Pero el resurgimiento del euroescepticismo supone una limitación en este caso", añadió. El rendimiento de los bonos del Estado alemán a 10 años , referencia de la zona euro, bajaba 1,5 puntos básicos, hasta el 3,40%, mientras la demanda de bonos refugio sostenía sus precios. El rendimiento se ha movido entre aproximadamente el 3,40% y el 3,50% desde principios de este mes. El rendimiento del bono alemán a dos años , más sensible a las expectativas sobre las tasas de interés oficiales, subía un punto básico, hasta el 3,05%.

item.title: Roche supera estimativas de receita, mas ações caem à medida que genéricos corroem vendas do Xolair
item.description: A farmacêutica suíça Roche superou as expectativas de vendas do terceiro trimestre nesta quinta-feira, impulsionada pela demanda constante por medicamentos-chave, como o Ocrevus, para ganhar tempo enquanto busca no exterior reabastecer seu pipeline diante de expirações iminentes de patentes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A farmacêutica suíça Roche (ROPC.S) superou as expectativas de vendas do terceiro trimestre nesta quinta-feira, impulsionada pela demanda constante por medicamentos-chave, como o Ocrevus, para ganhar tempo enquanto busca no exterior reabastecer seu pipeline diante de expirações iminentes de patentes. A receita do grupo cresceu 7% a taxas de câmbio constantes, atingindo 16,13 bilhões de francos suíços (US$19,61 bilhões), superando a previsão consensual elaborada pela empresa, de 15,75 bilhões de francos (US$19,15 bilhões). No entanto, o trimestre trouxe um sinal precoce de pressão competitiva — as vendas do medicamento Xolair ficaram abaixo das previsões do mercado após o lançamento do primeiro genérico mais barato, gerando vendas de 848 milhões de francos (US$1,03 bilhão) contra expectativas de 925 milhões de francos (US$1,12 bilhão). As ações caíam 1,1% no pregão da manhã. Com vários medicamentos de grande sucesso mais antigos se aproximando do vencimento das patentes, a Roche aposta em seus principais produtos para impulsionar o crescimento no curto prazo, ao mesmo tempo em que intensifica as negociações externas para tratamentos de última geração. A empresa fechou um acordo no valor de mais de US$15 bilhões com a chinesa Hansoh Pharma, segundo notícia divulgada na segunda-feira. Com foco no ecossistema de biotecnologia da Europa, o presidente-executivo Thomas Schinecker afirmou na quinta-feira que cerca de 50% dos acordos de licenciamento externos do grupo nos últimos quatro anos foram firmados nos EUA e os outros 50% na China e na Ásia. “Isso mostra um pouco a situação em que a Europa se encontra em termos de inovação”, disse Schinecker. A administração também observou que o impacto negativo das reformas nos preços dos serviços de saúde na China estava diminuindo, apesar das quedas de dois dígitos no país, com a divisão de diagnósticos — que cresceu 5%, para 3,54 bilhões de francos — devendo retornar a um crescimento “normal” na faixa de um dígito médio a alto no próximo ano. A Roche também se beneficiou da estabilização do dólar em relação ao franco suíço, aliviando o impacto prolongado das taxas de câmbio no mercado norte-americano, que responde por quase metade da receita do grupo. Os medicamentos mais vendidos impulsionaram a unidade farmacêutica, liderada pela injeção para esclerose múltipla Ocrevus, cuja receita cresceu 9% em moedas constantes, atingindo 1,84 bilhão de francos.

item.title: SAP clients increasingly worry about AI models' origin, CFO says
item.description: Customers are increasingly asking where the AI inside their business software was built, SAP's finance chief told Reuters on Thursday, with export controls and Europe's sovereignty debate now shaping decisions once made on price and performance alone.
item.dc:creator: Leo Marchandon
item.content:encoded: Customers are increasingly asking where the AI inside their business software was built, SAP's (SAPG.DE) finance chief told Reuters on Thursday, with export controls and Europe's sovereignty debate now shaping decisions once made on price and performance alone. "Could data used by that model be channelled out to end up in places where it shouldn't end up?" Dominik Asam said in the interview, describing a client question SAP regularly hears. It has become an art form to understand companies' precise requirements over technology governance when juggling several AI models, he added. SAP, Europe's most valuable tech company, embeds more than 70 models from various providers into its software that runs accounting and supply chains at many of the world's largest companies, a strategic choice to be agnostic on the market rather than internally build its own models. But for clients, where the AI comes from matters. A US customer may not accept components developed with Chinese models, while others' back-office work, including SAP's own, can run on open-weight software "from wherever it comes from", Asam said. "If you're a Department of Defense of a large nation, you will think about that differently as opposed to a mom-and-pop shop." [USN:S8N3UV03C TEXT:"European debate"] over a possible "kill switch" in US cloud infrastructure has also fed the market for sovereign alternatives, Asam said. SAP has recently signed deals with governments and defence contractors, and prefers access to models from every region, including Europe and Canada, so it can offer a flexible portfolio to such clients, he said. Asked whether this week's [USN:FWN4661WD TEXT:"PHP vulnerability"] disclosures had touched SAP, Asam said the company was using frontier AI models to attack and test its own products before anyone else could do it. "Anyone who says I don't have any vulnerabilities would lie to you," he said, while declining to comment on findings of such screenings.

item.title: Nasdaq futures drop over 1% as AI worries resurface, oil climbs
item.description: Nasdaq futures slid more than 1% on Thursday as high-growth stocks faced renewed pressure after earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms did little to allay concerns over AI spending, while a rebound in oil prices further dampened sentiment.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nasdaq futures slid more than 1% on Thursday as high-growth stocks faced renewed pressure after earnings from Tesla and Meta Platforms did little to allay concerns over AI spending, while a rebound in oil prices further dampened sentiment. The weakness follows a strong session on Wednesday when the tech-heavy Nasdaq led Wall Street higher as robust results from SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Super Micro (SMCI.O) rekindled optimism around AI-linked stocks. SpaceX dropped 2.3% and Super Micro fell 4.7% in premarket trading on Thursday as investors shifted their focus from earnings to the mounting cost of the AI buildout. Tesla (TSLA.O) fell 5.3% after the [USN:L4N4671SD TEXT:"electric-vehicle maker"] cut its annual capital expenditure forecast, raising questions about the pace of its AI and robotics expansion. Meta's (META.O) shares slipped 1.9% after the social media giant introduced new non-voting shares to help fund its costly AI push, reviving investor scrutiny of the substantial capital required to stay competitive in the race. The 'Magnificent 7' stocks were also down, with Amazon.com (AMZN.O) declining 1.6% and Nvidia (NVDA.O) down 2.4%. Chip stocks dropped, too. Intel (INTC.O) was down 5.1%, while AMD (AMD.O) , Qualcomm (QCOM.O) , Marvell Technology (MRVL.O) , Broadcom (AVGO.O) and Micron Technology (MU.O) slipped between 2.9% and 5.3%. At 04:56 a.m. ET, Dow E-minis were down 367 points, or 0.69%, S&P 500 E-minis were down 85.5 points, or 1.1%, and Nasdaq 100 E-minis were down 578.5 points, or 1.93%. Brent crude climbed more than 3% to $112 a barrel, near a five-month high, after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions and a wider Middle East conflict. A flight to safety pushed the 10-year yield down to around 5.085%. Bitcoin fell 3.4%, reflecting a broader risk-off mood as investors sought safer-haven assets. Later in the day, earnings from Spotify (SPOT.N) , Blackstone (BX.N) , American Airlines (AAL.O) and Honeywell International (HON.O) are expected to offer a broader read on corporate performance across sectors. IBM (IBM.N) fell 5.7% even after raising annual software revenue forecast and reporting [USN:L4N4671T3 TEXT:"third-quarter"] ahead of Wall Street expectations.

item.title: Shark nicknamed 'Bukangi' foils rescue attempts, returns to South Korean canal
item.description: A shark that South Korean authorities spent hours guiding into the open sea has swum back into a canal in the port city of Busan, eluding a net that was meant to prevent her return.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Grether, Hyun Yi
item.content:encoded: A shark that South Korean authorities spent hours guiding into the open sea has swum back into a canal in the port city of Busan, eluding a net that was meant to prevent her return. The 3-meter-long (10-foot) shark, nicknamed "Bukangi" after the Korean name for Busan's North Port, has become a viral sensation since she was spotted in the canal late last month, attracting 1.6 million visitors, according to the Busan Infrastructure Corporation. Authorities have so far made three attempts to encourage her to return to the open sea, the latest of which was on Wednesday involving floating platforms, nets, and divers. On Wednesday, after a month in the canal, Bukangi was successfully guided back into the open sea, according to the oceans ministry. But on Thursday, the ministry said that the shark had swum under one of the nets installed in the canal to be caught between the outer net and an inner net installed 30 to 40 meters deeper into the waterway. Officials have opened the outer net and reinforced barriers to prevent the shark from retreating further, in hopes that Bukangi would move out into the open water, they said. Experts said no further efforts to guide Bukangi out to the open sea are necessary, as the shark’s condition is stable. Authorities will continue to monitor her condition, the ministry added. South Korea's National Institute of Fisheries Science has identified Bukangi as a female dusky shark. The shark's prolonged stay has raised environmental concerns, with experts pointing to warming ocean temperatures as the cause of more frequent shark sightings along South Korea's east coast. Dusky sharks are classified as endangered by the International Union for Conservation of Nature.

item.title: Far-left leader Melenchon in firing line as France blame-game heats up
item.description: Rivals from the centre-left to the far right have turned on Jean-Luc Melenchon and his France Unbowed (LFI) party, accusing them of fuelling France's worst civil unrest in years.
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose, Elizabeth Pineau
item.content:encoded: Rivals from the centre-left to the far right have turned on Jean-Luc Melenchon and his France Unbowed (LFI) party, accusing them of fuelling France's worst civil unrest in years. Melenchon, who launched his fourth presidential bid in May and remains the hard left's strongest hope of reaching next year's election run-off, has faced mounting criticism since unrest engulfed several French cities, with opponents saying years of confrontational rhetoric helped fuel tensions now spilling onto the streets. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu sharpened those attacks on Tuesday, telling an LFI lawmaker that the party's "political agenda of instilling violence and chaos in the country was now on full display". The 75-year-old leader has rejected suggestions that LFI bears responsibility for the unrest, accusing the government instead of failing to address deep-rooted social and economic grievances in France's poorer suburbs. But criticism has come from across the political spectrum. Gerard Larcher, the president of the Senate, told Le Figaro this week it was worth considering whether LFI should be banned, a suggestion decried as "authoritarian" by LFI. Laurent Jacobelli, a spokesperson for Marine Le Pen's National Rally (RN), blamed "the ultra-left, including France Unbowed", as well as what he called uncontrolled immigration, for creating a revolutionary climate. Marc Fesneau, of centrist party MoDem, said Melenchon had long promoted the idea that "everything must be a battleground". "When you turn everything into a confrontation, you run serious risks," Fesneau told Reuters. The attacks underscore both Melenchon's central place in French politics and the unease he provokes as the country heads toward a presidential election expected to pit increasingly strong anti-establishment forces against a [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"weakened political centre"]. The unrest has reinforced that contrast, shifting scrutiny onto the hard left while allowing Le Pen to strike a more presidential tone on law and order, an issue that traditionally favours [USN:L8N4611KF TEXT:"the far right"]. Yet with France's political landscape fragmented into three rival blocs and traditional centre-left and centre-right parties struggling, analysts say Melenchon remains a [USN:L5N2WU0KX TEXT:"formidable political force"]. YOUTH APPEAL AND THE 'NEW FRANCE' LFI has built its support by mobilising younger voters, many of whom have grown disillusioned with mainstream politics. An IFOP poll for LCI published this month put Melenchon on 16.5%, behind Le Pen's 36% but ahead of all other mainstream candidates. A Cluster17 poll found nearly half of 18-to-24-year-olds and more than a third of 25-to-34-year-olds would back Melenchon. That has made him a prominent voice for many students involved in the protest movement and [USN:L1N4610U5 TEXT:"wider unrest"] that has shaken France in recent weeks. However, Frederic Dabi, head of pollster IFOP, said the unrest risked reinforcing one of Melenchon's biggest electoral weaknesses: his inability to win over older voters. "The perception that Jean-Luc Melenchon has been too indulgent towards perpetrators of violence is an absolute red line for a large part of the electorate," Dabi said. Nevertheless, the party has also built [USN:L1N4250UE TEXT:"strong support in poorer urban areas"] and among many voters from immigrant backgrounds who see themselves reflected in Melenchon's vision of a "New France" — a multicultural republic that embraces ethnic and religious diversity and gives greater political representation to communities that often feel overlooked. Supporters say that reflects social realities rather than identity politics. "It's the unique synthesis between a programme of revolutionary rupture and the desire to govern the country," LFI lawmaker Hadrien Clouet told Reuters. Clouet said that meant tackling inequality and reversing a decades-long [USN:L8N44L1BW TEXT:"transfer of wealth towards finance"] and a narrow oligarchic elite. Yet critics say LFI often blurs the line between democratic protest and more radical political agitation. UPRISING LANGUAGE DRAWS SCRUTINY Melenchon has frequently invoked the [USN:L5N2WW5PF TEXT:"language of popular uprising"]. During the pensions crisis of 2023, he urged supporters to "tear down the citadel" of President Emmanuel Macron's government and has at times spoken favourably of "citizen insurrection" as a democratic force. Supporters say such language refers to mass political mobilisation, not violence. The party officially advocates non-violent action. LFI and its allies argue some of the accusations are politically motivated. This week, investigative news outlet Mediapart reported, citing an anonymous intelligence officer, that officials had been instructed to portray LFI as being behind the protest movement despite what the source described as a lack of evidence. The government denied the allegation. Still, opponents say Melenchon's messaging is often deliberately ambiguous. "They say they are against vandals, but at the same time they justify masks at demonstrations," said Sylvain Maillard of Macron's Renaissance party. "They never calm things down. They always say it's the police's fault. They want chaos." Former Socialist President Francois Hollande, however, warned against making Melenchon the sole focus of the debate. "It is not one political party or one individual that poured fuel on the fire," Hollande told France Inter. While criticising LFI for sometimes drawing an equivalence between rioter violence and police violence, he said: "To fixate on LFI is to fail to see what is happening in the country."

item.title: Turquía acogerá a los ministros de Exteriores europeos para tratar los conflictos regionales
item.description: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores turco, Hakan Fidan, recibirá este viernes en Estambul a sus homólogos de Egipto, Pakistán, Arabia Saudita, Reino Unido, Francia y Alemania para mantener conversaciones sobre los conflictos regionales, dijo el jueves una fuente diplomática turca.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores turco, Hakan Fidan, recibirá este viernes en Estambul a sus homólogos de Egipto, Pakistán, Arabia Saudita, Reino Unido, Francia y Alemania para mantener conversaciones sobre los conflictos regionales, dijo el jueves una fuente diplomática turca. Los siete países se reunirán en este formato por primera vez, por iniciativa de Turquía, según la fuente, en un momento en que las guerras que afectan a Irán, Yemen y Ucrania amenazan las rutas marítimas y la seguridad regional. Se espera que los ministros debatan la cuestión israelí-palestina, la situación más reciente en el estrecho de Ormuz, los acontecimientos relacionados con Yemen, los esfuerzos para poner fin a la guerra entre Rusia y Ucrania, y las oportunidades para una cooperación más estrecha entre los países de la región y los europeos, añadió la misma fuente. Se espera que Fidan haga hincapié en la necesidad de una solución diplomática a la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, en la importancia de la libertad de navegación en los estrechos de Ormuz y Bab el-Mandeb, y que reitere el apoyo de Turquía a la seguridad de Arabia Saudita frente a los ataques de los milicianos hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, en el marco del Acuerdo de Defensa Conjunta de La Meca firmado entre Turquía, Pakistán y Arabia Saudita, según la fuente. Asimismo, comunicará a sus homólogos que Turquía ha estado trabajando para evitar que la guerra en Ucrania se extienda al mar Negro, señalando los riesgos para la seguridad regional que plantea el conflicto, añadió la fuente.

item.title: Xi pide una mejora cualitativa y un crecimiento medible de la economía china
item.description: El presidente de China, Xi Jinping, instó a lograr una mejora cualitativa efectiva y un crecimiento cuantitativo razonable de la economía en un discurso pronunciado el jueves, informó Xinhua.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de China, Xi Jinping, instó a lograr una mejora cualitativa efectiva y un crecimiento cuantitativo razonable de la economía en un discurso pronunciado el jueves, informó Xinhua. "Debemos impulsar con determinación un desarrollo de alta calidad y satisfacer continuamente las crecientes necesidades del pueblo de una vida mejor", dijo Xi al referirse a la promoción del progreso social integral sin dejar de mantener la estabilidad. También destacó la necesidad de mantener el "liderazgo absoluto" del Partido Comunista de China sobre las fuerzas armadas y avanzar en el "fortalecimiento político del Ejército", informó la agencia estatal de noticias. El dirigente mencionó la reforma de las fuerzas armadas y su fortalecimiento mediante la ciencia y la tecnología, así como el talento y una gestión conforme a la ley. El discurso formó parte de las conmemoraciones del 90º aniversario de la Larga Marcha, una serie de retiradas del Ejército Rojo, liderado por Mao Zedong, para eludir la persecución de las fuerzas nacionalistas de Chiang Kai-shek en 1934 y 1935.

item.title: China Evergrande liquidators recover 1% of debt claims after 2-1/2 years
item.description: China Evergrande Group's liquidators have recovered $435.9 million from asset sales and loan recoveries so far, highlighting the challenge of repaying creditors with claims of about $46 billion against the developer.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China Evergrande Group's liquidators have recovered $435.9 million from asset sales and loan recoveries so far, highlighting the challenge of repaying creditors with claims of about $46 billion against the developer. In their second progress report since a Hong Kong court ordered Evergrande's liquidation in January 2024, the liquidators, Edward Middleton and Tiffany Wong of Alvarez & Marsal, said on Thursday they aimed to make a first interim dividend payment to creditors in the first half of 2027, although the amount has yet to be determined. Evergrande, once China's top property developer, defaulted on most of its roughly $300 billion in liabilities and became a symbol of the property crisis that has weighed on the world's second-largest economy. The liquidators said they had raised the $435.9 million through the sale of assets including aircraft, artwork and club memberships, as well as the settlement of loan receivables. They said 96 of the 107 artworks found at Evergrande's Hong Kong headquarters had been sold for $28.8 million at a loss. The collection included works by Picasso, Monet and Warhol, as well as sculptures by Moore and Hepworth. Other assets being sold include a private jet expected to fetch about $12 million in the fourth quarter. The liquidators are also seeking a $2 million refund from a US university for part of a donation made in 2020. The liquidators have taken control of more than 100 Evergrande subsidiaries across multiple jurisdictions, but said prospects for recovering assets held by mainland Chinese subsidiaries were "considered remote". In August, Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan, 67, was sentenced to life imprisonment by a Chinese court, which also ordered the confiscation of his personal assets. Industry experts say Evergrande's liquidation could take more than a decade to complete given the scale and complexity of the group.
