item.title: Barclays vai cortar 5.000 empregos em iniciativa de redução de custos impulsionada pela IA
item.description: O Barclays anunciou que cortará cerca de 5.000 empregos, ou 5% de sua força de trabalho, este ano, à medida que utiliza tecnologias como a inteligência artificial para reduzir custos fixos e melhorar a rentabilidade geral.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Barclays (BARC.L) anunciou que cortará cerca de 5.000 empregos, ou 5% de sua força de trabalho, este ano, à medida que utiliza tecnologias como a inteligência artificial para reduzir custos fixos e melhorar a rentabilidade geral. Os cortes de pessoal foram apresentados quando o Barclays divulgou lucro no terceiro trimestre de 2,3 bilhões de libras (3,08 bilhões de dólares), acima do registrado no ano anterior, mas abaixo das previsões dos analistas, devido ao desempenho abaixo do esperado do negócio de negociação de renda fixa. O banco informou ter realizado mais 201 milhões de libras em “medidas de redução de custos estruturais” no terceiro trimestre, como parte de seu plano de longo prazo para reduzir despesas, como custos com pessoal, por meio de maior uso de tecnologia. Cerca de 60% do total de cortes de pessoal afetará funcionários em funções de apoio, como desenvolvedores, disse a diretora financeira Anna Cross aos repórteres, em um dos sinais mais claros até agora, vindo de um grande banco, de como a IA está permitindo que as empresas reduzam o quadro de funcionários nessas funções. Cross disse que 1.000 cargos já foram eliminados, com o restante a ser cortado até o final do ano. As ações do Barclays caíam 2,5% no início do pregão, apresentando desempenho inferior ao de outras instituições financeiras (.SX7P) . As ações do banco caíram 14% neste ano, em linha com os pares europeus, que sofreram correção após anos de alta, à medida que as taxas de juros mais elevadas impulsionaram os lucros. A Shore Capital afirmou em uma nota que os resultados ficaram abaixo do esperado devido ao desempenho decepcionante do banco de investimentos. O banco de investimentos do Barclays registrou receita total no terceiro trimestre de 3,1 bilhões de libras, abaixo das previsões de 3,3 bilhões de libras. Os resultados do terceiro trimestre dos concorrentes do Barclays em Wall Street, divulgados no início deste mês, mostraram a natureza cíclica da receita dos bancos de investimento, à medida que as negociações desaceleraram e as mesas de renda fixa apresentaram desempenho abaixo do esperado, com apenas a negociação de ações mantendo o forte ímpeto observado no primeiro semestre do ano. (Reportagem de Lawrence White)

item.title: US extends deadline for buyers of Lukoil foreign assets until November 21
item.description: The US has extended the deadline for companies to negotiate with Russian oil major Lukoil about buying its foreign assets until November 21, according to the US Office of Foreign Assets Control.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The US has extended the deadline for companies to negotiate with Russian oil major Lukoil (LKOH.MM) about buying its foreign assets until November 21, according to the US Office of Foreign Assets Control. The deadline was extended after the US private equity firm Carlyle Group [USN:L1N45V07F TEXT:"dropped"] its bid earlier this month. Washington imposed sanctions in October 2025 on Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer, and Rosneft (ROSN.MM) , its top producer, to reduce Moscow's ability to pay for its military campaign in Ukraine . Lukoil's assets were put up for sale last year, while Rosneft has not announced any divestments. Carlyle had [USN:L1N3YU0AY TEXT:"initially agreed"] on January 29 to buy Lukoil's assets, excluding those in Kazakhstan. The fund was in talks to partner with Abu Dhabi-based funds Mubadala, XRG and IHC, as well as the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation for the deal, according to people familiar with the matter. The Lukoil portfolio, initially valued at around $22 billion, had attracted interest from at least a dozen companies including Exxon Mobil (XOM.N) and the former owner of Pornhub, Bernd Bergmair.

item.title: ATP blocks 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players, fans
item.description: Social media abuse was directed at over 85% of men's tennis players attracting engagement online in the past year, with the ATP blocking some 234,000 comments from reaching them or fans, the governing body said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Social media abuse was directed at over 85% of men's tennis players attracting engagement online in the past year, with the ATP blocking some 234,000 comments from reaching them or fans, the governing body said on Thursday. The ATP based the findings on an analysis of more than 3.7 million comments across ATP and player social media channels by its Safe Sport initiative, which uses AI-enabled moderation and specialist threat assessment. It said more than 284,000 abusive comments were identified, and over 82% of them were removed in real time. During its [USN:L4N3UD0GR TEXT:"first year"], the programme identified and hid upwards of 162,000 comments containing "severe" abuse. "Player welfare sits at the heart of the ATP's safeguarding work," said Andrew Azzopardi, the ATP director of safeguarding. "Preventing more than 234,000 abusive comments from reaching players and fans demonstrates the tangible impact the programme is having every day. Online abuse has no place in tennis. "We will keep investing in the technology, expertise and partnerships that protect players, and we will continue working with the authorities to hold those responsible to account." ANONYMOUS ABUSERS Tennis players, like many athletes, often have to deal with the wrath of anonymous abusers online, many of whom are [USN:L6N43I0IJ TEXT:"bettors"], with French player Gael Monfils humorously hitting back at some of them following an early defeat in Stuttgart last year. Monfils, 40, said at the time he was surprised people still put money on him to win against much younger opponents. Online abuse is not confined to [USN:L4N3TY0AE TEXT:"angry gamblers"], with American [USN:L1N45T0DY TEXT:"Coco Gauff"] saying earlier this month she received an "insane" amount of racist abuse at the China Open, [USN:L6N45X03Y TEXT:"prompting condemnation"] from the United Nations Human Rights Office. World Tennis, the WTA, the All England Club and the United States Tennis Association have launched monitoring services that use a combination of artificial intelligence and open-source data to help protect players. The French Open has also made AI-powered software available for players to block online harassment and hate speech.

item.title: The Azores are showing the world what ocean leadership looks like
item.description: When I was a child, no ship could take cameras, let alone humans, into the deep ocean to see the extraordinary life below. We knew little about the world under the surface of the sea. Today, we can explore seamounts, observe deep-sea creatures in their own homes, and ask questions that were unimaginable even a generation ago.
item.dc:creator: Sylvia Earle
item.content:encoded: When I was a child, no ship could take cameras, let alone humans, into the deep ocean to see the extraordinary life below. We knew little about the world under the surface of the sea. Today, we can explore seamounts, observe deep-sea creatures in their own homes, and ask questions that were unimaginable even a generation ago. Yet the more we learn about the ocean, the more we understand the magnitude of how much remains to be explored and the urgency of protecting the vast living realm that has shaped and maintains the habitability of Earth. I was reminded of this recently in the Azores, an autonomous region of nine islands that lie in 1,500 kilometres off the coast of Portugal, where I had the honour of becoming godmother to the Azores Ocean, a new research vessel. To me, the beauty of a ship is not simply in its appearance, but in what it can do. This vessel gives scientists new ways to investigate the Atlantic and bring its hidden wonders into view. And there is no better place for us to do that than in the Azores, which in October 2024 established the Azores Marine Park , a marine protected area covering 287,000 square kilometres, the largest MPA in the North Atlantic. Half of the area is fully protected and the other half is “highly protected”. While nations around the world have committed to protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030 , only around 10% is currently protected, well below that target. The fact that the Azores have already taken a major step towards the 30% goal is something worth celebrating, and an example worth following. Dr Sylvia Earle, right, during a dive at Midway Atoll National Wildlife Refuge in the North Pacific. Amanda Meyer/USFWS/Handout via REUTERS The Azores are also part of something much larger. Through the charity I founded, Mission Blue , these islands and their surrounding waters are recognised as a Hope Spot, one of a growing global network of special places critical to the health of the ocean. Hope Spots are championed by people who understand that protecting the ocean begins with recognising its value and taking protective actions. Their conservation effort did not happen overnight. Scientists working in the Azores have spent decades investigating the waters around these islands, revealing deep-sea habitats, remarkable biodiversity and the vulnerabilities of marine life. Their discoveries helped build the knowledge base that the Azores government needed to establish the MPA two years ago. The new vessel represents a major investment in the next chapter of that work. The technology on board is extraordinary, but it is the people asking questions, making discoveries and seeking to understand the ocean who will give it purpose. And in the Azores, there are world-class scientists who have dedicated years of their lives to doing just that. We are living at once in the greatest era of ocean exploration and a time of profound loss. Now we know what our predecessors did not and could not know. The ocean is Earth's life-support system. It shapes our climate, generates much of the oxygen we breathe and sustains life from microscopic organisms to the great whales that frequent Azorean waters. Caring for it is not an optional luxury. For too long, we have behaved as though the ocean were too vast to harm and too resilient to fail. We have learned otherwise within my lifetime. The same knowledge that reveals the damage also gives us a remarkable opportunity to choose a different path. The Azores show what can happen when scientific knowledge is met with the determination to act. Research matters. So do the decisions made by leaders, the participation of communities and the people whose livelihoods are tied to the sea. The Azores Ocean, a new research vessel.which is enabling scientists to find new ways to investigate the Atlantic. Marinha Portuguesa/Handout via REUTERS In fact, 100% of humankind and all living things depend on the ocean for our existence. And protection must mean more than lines on a map. Effective management, monitoring, communication, and enforcement are what turn a designation into lasting conservation. From the Azores to communities across the world, Hope Spots bring together people, science, and a shared commitment to protecting the places that matter most to the ocean's future. Each Hope Spot has its own challenges and opportunities, but together they demonstrate how local action can contribute to global change. In Rio de Janeiro, for example, a new 3,000-hectare marine protected area has been established safeguarding important fish nursery habitats and ecosystems supporting traditional coastal communities, supported in part through Rolex's Perpetual Planet Initiative. In California, the Chumash Indigenous community supported the creation of the Point Sal MPA , which falls within the Chumash Heritage National Marine Sanctuary Hope Spot. The MPA was approved following three years of advocacy by tribal leaders, scientists and coastal communities, safeguarding the area’s marine habitats indefinitely from seabed mining and oil drilling. The people of the Azores, however determined, cannot protect the ocean alone. But they have demonstrated that ambitious protection can move from aspiration to reality. They have shown that positive change is possible. Children today inherit unprecedented knowledge and unique opportunities to choose an enduring future. With knowing comes caring, and with caring, there is hope for actions that will ensure an enduring, prosperous future. The ocean keeps us alive. It is time to act as though our lives depend on protecting it. Because they do.

item.title: Meta coloca agente Muse no centro de estratégia de IA; planeja novas ações para impulsionar investimentos
item.description: A Meta lançou na quarta-feira novas ações sem direito a voto para ajudar a financiar a expansão em IA da gigante das redes sociais, enquanto os executivos apresentaram sua visão de organizar o futuro da empresa em torno do negócio emergente de agentes de IA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Meta lançou na quarta-feira novas ações sem direito a voto para ajudar a financiar a expansão em IA da gigante das redes sociais, enquanto os executivos apresentaram sua visão de organizar o futuro da empresa em torno do negócio emergente de agentes de IA. As ações da controladora do Facebook e do Instagram subiam mais de 4% no pregão prolongado. A Meta também previu uma receita no quarto trimestre acima das estimativas de Wall Street e divulgou um forte crescimento de seu novo aplicativo de agente de IA para consumidores, o Muse. A empresa vem investindo pesadamente em chips avançados e centros de dados para competir de forma mais agressiva com os líderes do mercado de IA, OpenAI e Anthropic, impulsionando-a para a vanguarda de uma corrida emergente por agentes de IA para consumidores, ao mesmo tempo em que corrói seu fluxo de caixa livre. A Meta emitirá uma nova classe de ações ordinárias Classe C sem direito a voto em janeiro de 2027, resultando efetivamente em um desdobramento de duas por uma, para financiar aquisições e reter os melhores talentos, mantendo ao mesmo tempo o controle do presidente-executivo Mark Zuckerberg. Zuckerberg afirmou que mais de 10 milhões de pessoas nos EUA e no Canadá criaram contas no Muse em um mês e meio e que o crescimento continua forte. CUSTOS MAIS ALTOS Ainda assim, Zuckerberg reconheceu que os custos de oferecer o Muse eram mais altos do que aqueles associados a muitos outros novos produtos da Meta ao longo dos anos e disse que passaria a monetizar o agente “um pouco mais cedo do que o previsto em nosso plano normal”. A diretora financeira, Susan Li, previu que os negócios de IA da Meta começariam a gerar receita incremental em 2027 e se tornariam “uma fonte significativa de diversificação de receita ao longo do tempo”. Os executivos também enfatizaram que a IA seria o foco daqui para frente para a unidade Reality Labs da Meta, que vem registrando prejuízos e liderou a iniciativa da Meta de construir o “Metaverso”, um mundo digital imersivo que inspirou a mudança de nome do Facebook para Meta em 2021. A Meta elevou o limite inferior de sua previsão de gastos anuais, esperando agora que os gastos de capital fiquem entre US$135 bilhões e US$145 bilhões este ano, acima dos US$130 bilhões a US$145 bilhões previstos anteriormente. A receita do terceiro trimestre ficou acima do esperado, em US$64,60 bilhões, superando as estimativas de Wall Street de US$63,37 bilhões, de acordo com dados compilados pela LSEG. A empresa também projetou uma receita para o quarto trimestre entre US$73 bilhões e US$76 bilhões, acima das estimativas de US$73,73 bilhões. (Reportagem de Jaspreet Singh em Bengaluru e Katie Paul em Nova York)

item.title: Havells India posts quarterly profit rise on strong cables demand
item.description: Consumer electronics and power distribution equipment maker Havells India reported a nearly 10% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, helped by strong demand across its portfolio that spans wires, cables and home appliances.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Consumer electronics and power distribution equipment maker Havells India (HVEL.NS) reported a nearly 10% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, helped by strong demand across its portfolio that spans wires, cables and home appliances. Consolidated net profit rose to 3.50 billion rupees ($36.89 million) in the quarter ended September 30 from 3.19 billion rupees a year earlier Revenue jumped 34.6% to 64.32 billion rupees Demand for electrical and infrastructure-linked products remained strong in the quarter The cables business, Havells' largest segment, posted nearly 48% revenue growth, aided by commodity-linked price increases and a shift toward higher-sized cables, the company said Investments in housing and power networks continued to support sales in the segment Havells said consumption demand remained steady despite elevated inflation, while healthy operating leverage helped drive a 30.5% rise in EBITDA However, volatility in aluminium prices weighed on margins in the cables business ($1 = 94.8100 Indian rupees)

item.title: As Americans eat out less, paper towel maker Essity feels the pinch
item.description: Essity is seeing greater weakness among the US restaurants it supplies than the European ones, the CEO of the Swedish hygiene products maker said on Thursday, as rising prices and a slowing jobs market put pressure on American household budgets.
item.dc:creator: Vera Dvorakova, Jesus Calero
item.content:encoded: Essity (ESSITYa.ST) is seeing greater weakness among the US restaurants it supplies than the European ones, the CEO of the Swedish hygiene products maker said on Thursday, as rising prices and a slowing jobs market put pressure on American household budgets. "Consumers are not going out to restaurants as much as they do in Europe," Ulrika Kolsrud told Reuters. The trend is hitting Essity's professional hygiene business, which sells products such as Tork paper towels to restaurants and other businesses, and generates 40% of its revenue in the US. The unit's sales, volumes and prices all fell in the third quarter, and Essity also flagged higher costs of goods sold. Kolsrud's comments reflect the strain faced by US consumers, whose wages are struggling to keep pace with [USN:L1N45Z0VZ TEXT:"inflation"] while companies [USN:L1N45N170 TEXT:"pull back"] on hiring. US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September from a year earlier, outpacing average hourly wage growth of 3.0% over the past 12 months. Meanwhile, employers excluding farms added just 29,000 jobs during the month. A Gallup survey published on Wednesday showed that only 39% of Americans ate at restaurants at least once a week, down from 53% in 2019. Consumer goods companies have been walking a fine line between raising prices to offset higher input costs and protecting demand after several years of inflation-driven hikes. Essity management said it was again raising prices across business areas to offset higher raw material and energy costs, having previously lowered them in some categories. The pressure from higher prices is the sharpest at the lower end of the income scale. The latest Federal Reserve survey, covering 2022 to 2025, [USN:L6N45V0Q8 TEXT:"showed"] that income gains for the less well-off did little to build wealth, and net worth for the bottom fourth of households fell by more than 50%.

item.title: Greece says it is implementing sanctions linked to Iran
item.description: The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Greek finance ministry said on Thursday it was implementing sanctions in place linked to Iran and that it backed efforts to effectively combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism. The statement comes after the US Treasury Department said on Wednesday it imposed sanctions on Karnakis & Karnakis, a law firm based in Greece and Panama, saying it had for years provided legal assistance to Iranian shipping networks. The Treasury also said that the US Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued [USN:L1N4670VZ TEXT:"an administrative subpoena"] to advance an investigation into a Greek bank, which it did not name. The Greek finance ministry said it had taken note of the US Treasury statement, adding that "all available information is being evaluated, and appropriate measures are being taken in accordance with established procedures and applicable national, EU, and international law."

item.title: India's JSW Paints eyes 4, 5-year debt to refinance acquisition-led funding, bankers say
item.description: India's JSW Paints is likely to raise funds through issuance of bonds maturing in four years and five years and should go ahead with the sale in the next couple of weeks, two merchant bankers with direct knowledge of the matter said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Dharamraj Dhutia
item.content:encoded: India's JSW Paints is likely to raise funds through issuance of bonds maturing in four years and five years and should go ahead with the sale in the next couple of weeks, two merchant bankers with direct knowledge of the matter said on Thursday. The company could look to raise around 30 billion rupees ($316.56 million), the bankers said. The bankers requested anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to media. JSW Paints did not reply to a Reuters email seeking comment. The proceeds of the latest debt issuance are likely to be used for the refinancing of an earlier fundraise the company put towards its acquisition of Akzo Nobel India last year, the bankers added. In November 2025, JSW Paints had raised 33 billion rupees through sale of five-year bonds, which were directly placed with large foreign banks and foreign investors. These bonds had a put option at the end of a year. Indian companies have been turning to the bond market to fund acquisitions in recent months, driven by robust demand from investors that's contributing to what [USN:L4N4620TZ TEXT:"may become a record year"] for corporate debt issuance in the country. ($1 = 94.7675 Indian rupees)

item.title: Russia-linked hackers used decentralised network in Ukraine cyberattack, ESET says
item.description: Russia-linked hackers used a decentralised volunteer-run network to conceal communications during an attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics company, marking the first documented case of a state-linked group using the network this way, ESET researchers said.
item.dc:creator: Leo Marchandon
item.content:encoded: Russia-linked hackers used a decentralised volunteer-run network to conceal communications during an attack on a Ukrainian grain logistics company, marking the first documented case of a state-linked group using the network this way, ESET researchers said. The attack culminated in the destruction of data at the company in September 2025. Researchers say the technique could make hacking operations harder to identify and disrupt because decentralised networks do not rely on a single centrally controlled server. Agriculture accounted for roughly a fifth of Ukraine's economy and nearly half its [USN:L8N46305V TEXT:"exports"] before the war, according to research estimates, and Russia has targeted the sector throughout the conflict, bombing ports, grain elevators and fields. Slovakia-based cybersecurity firm ESET said the attackers gained access to the company's systems in July 2025 through a phishing email carrying a malicious attachment. The attackers later installed software that allowed them to remotely control compromised computers, browse files, take screenshots and steal documents before data was wiped from the company's systems on Sept. 17, 2025. ESET attributed the data destruction to Sandworm, a hacking group widely linked to Russian military intelligence and previously blamed for cyberattacks on Ukrainian and [USN:L6N3YO13R TEXT:"Polish"] power grids. The malicious software communicated through a server hidden inside Yggdrasil, an experimental volunteer-run network with no central owner, the first use of such a network that ESET has documented by a state-linked group. ESET said it believed one Russia-linked hacking group gained the initial access before handing control to Sandworm, although it could not determine which group operated the newly identified malware. The firm did not identify the victim company.

item.title: Italia y España levantan los controles fronterizos impuestos tras la llegada de migrantes a Ceuta
item.description: Italia y España han acordado levantar los controles fronterizos para los ciudadanos de ambos países, dijo el jueves el Ministerio del Interior italiano, poniendo fin a una disputa de tres meses desencadenada por la afluencia de migrantes al enclave español de Ceuta.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italia y España han acordado levantar los controles fronterizos para los ciudadanos de ambos países, dijo el jueves el Ministerio del Interior italiano, poniendo fin a una disputa de tres meses desencadenada por la afluencia de migrantes al enclave español de Ceuta. El Gobierno de derechas italiano suspendió por primera vez sus acuerdos de fronteras abiertas con España el 31 de julio y alegó que quería asegurarse de que ningún migrante que entrara en Ceuta pudiera continuar su viaje hacia su territorio. Madrid respondió tomando medidas similares contra Roma y calificó la decisión italiana de "injusta, contraria a los intereses de la UE, y discriminatoria para la población española". Los ministros del Interior de Italia y España mantuvieron una conversación telefónica y acordaron no prorrogar la suspensión de los acuerdos de Schengen de fronteras abiertas de la Unión Europea, según el comunicado italiano. "La decisión, tomada tras una cuidadosa evaluación de la situación, irá acompañada de medidas reforzadas de intercambio de información para garantizar la plena seguridad del espacio común de Schengen", añadió el ministerio.

item.title: More LaLiga clubs join pact to cap ticket prices for away fans
item.description: Three more clubs in Spain's top division have joined an agreement to cap away ticket prices at a maximum of €30 ($34), a spokesperson for LaLiga told Reuters on Thursday, meaning 17 clubs in the 20-team league now participate.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Three more clubs in Spain's top division have joined an agreement to cap away ticket prices at a maximum of €30 ($34), a spokesperson for LaLiga told Reuters on Thursday, meaning 17 clubs in the 20-team league now participate. LaLiga is strengthening the reciprocal agreement between clubs as [USN:L6N467107 TEXT:"AC Milan fans boycott their visit to Udinese"] over away ticket prices of €65 ($73) The agreement, in place since the 2023-24 season, also ensures a minimum of 300 tickets are made available to travelling fans Away ticket sales have increased by 33% per game on average, according to LaLiga data. England's Premier League has a cap of £30 pounds ($40) for away fans. German's Bundesliga guarantees 10% of available capacity for away support, with their tickets matched to home prices. European governing body UEFA's regulations require 5% of stadium capacity to be allocated for away fans with a price cap of €50 ($56,20) in the Champions League The LaLiga spokesperson did not name the three additional Spanish teams joining the price cap scheme ($1 = 0.8898 euros)

item.title: BOURSE ID Logistics bondit de près de 10%, le T3 sur-performe en France comme à l'étranger
item.description: L'action ID Logistics bondit en Bourse jeudi, le groupe français de transport ayant fait état la veille d'une nette hausse de son chiffre d'affaires trimestriel, les investisseurs saluant la performance supérieure aux attentes et les perspectives de croissance.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'action ID Logistics bondit en Bourse jeudi, le groupe français de transport ayant fait état la veille d'une nette hausse de son chiffre d'affaires trimestriel, les investisseurs saluant la performance supérieure aux attentes et les perspectives de croissance. À Paris, vers 08h45 GMT, l'action se hisse en tête du SBF 120 (.SBF120) et décolle de 9,5% à 370 euros, l'indice reculant de 1,21% au même moment. Le groupe [USN:FWN467236 TEXT:"a publié"] mercredi soir un chiffre d'affaires en progression de 25,6% sur un an au troisième trimestre, à 1,17 milliard d'euros, et a cité dans un communiqué la dynamique commerciale portée par ses clients internationaux. "ID Logistics continue de surperformer quel que soit le contexte, y compris en France !", s'enthousiasme dans une note jeudi Florent Thy-tine, "Head of Equity Research" chez TP Icap Midcap, saluant une publication "une nouvelle fois plus que satisfaisante". Le courtier rappelle que l'activité d'ID Logistics en France ne représente plus que 20% de son activité, "et que même en France le groupe parvient à maintenir un niveau de croissance satisfaisant malgré un contexte compliqué". La croissance du groupe en Amérique du nord a bondi de 48,1% sur un an à données comparables, tandis que l’Europe hors France a grimpé de 23,4%. "ID Logistics est ainsi le dossier à avoir en portefeuille dans le contexte actuel", souligne Florent Thy-tine.

item.title: Turkey to host regional and European foreign ministers for talks on regional conflicts, source says
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will host his counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Britain, France and Germany in Istanbul on Friday for talks on regional conflicts, a Turkish diplomatic source said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan will host his counterparts from Egypt, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, Britain, France and Germany in Istanbul on Friday for talks on regional conflicts, a Turkish diplomatic source said on Thursday. The seven countries will meet in this format for the first time, at Turkey's initiative, the source said, as wars involving Iran, Yemen and Ukraine threaten shipping routes and regional security. The ministers are expected to discuss the Israeli-Palestinian issue, the latest situation in the Strait of Hormuz, developments related to Yemen, efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war, and opportunities for closer cooperation between the regional and European countries, the person added. Fidan is expected to emphasise the need for a diplomatic solution to the war between the United States and Iran, the importance of freedom of navigation in the straits of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb, and reiterate Turkey's [USN:L6N4670PY TEXT:"support for Saudi Arabia's security"] against attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi militants under the [USN:L6N4440IT TEXT:"Mecca Joint Defence Agreement"] signed between Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the source said. He will also tell counterparts that Turkey has been [USN:L6N45U0U5 TEXT:"working to stop"] the war in Ukraine spreading to the Black Sea, pointing to the regional security risks posed by the conflict, the source added.

item.title: Lula hopes older voters can help power him to victory against Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description: Rony Amaral, 71, is terrified right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro will slash healthcare and pension spending if he wins Sunday's runoff vote, so he is supporting leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva instead.
item.dc:creator: Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Rony Amaral, 71, is terrified right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro will slash healthcare and pension spending if he wins Sunday's runoff vote, so he is supporting leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva instead. Amaral and his 91-year-old mother Aisa form part of a growing cohort of voters in fast-ageing Brazil who could play a decisive role in the razor-tight election. Since 2010, the number of voters over 60 has grown by 74%, according to IBGE, the government statistics agency, and they today make up nearly 25% of Brazil's electorate, increasing their political weight. Polls show a growing share of them support Lula, who has overseen one of the largest and most generous welfare programs in Brazil's history during his three presidential terms. He is neck and neck with Bolsonaro going into Sunday's vote. "What I see is a fear among people over 60 that they will be left without care," Amaral said. "Even some on the right share this fear." According to pollster Quaest, Lula leads among seniors with 48% of voting intention. It found 42% plan on voting for Bolsonaro, who scores less highly than his father, ex-President Jair Bolsonaro, did among the same demographic at this stage in the 2022 presidential election. OVERLOOKED DEMOGRAPHIC Despite their growing importance, seniors have traditionally been overlooked in Brazilian campaigns, said Cila Schulman, chief executive of polling firm Ideia. Lula's campaign is now actively targeting the so-called "Lula generation" — seniors aged over 70, close in age to the 80-year-old president — hoping their support can help overcome the two-point gap between Bolsonaro and Lula in the first round. The party has launched a website aimed at seniors with the aim of persuading more older voters to go to the polls. "In the first round, I wasn't enthusiastic, but now that the race is so close, I'm going," said Ana dos Reis, 76, who lives in a low-income neighborhood in northern Sao Paulo. "Who knows, maybe my vote is what Lula needs to win?" FEAR OF LOSING WELFARE GAINS Unlike younger voters, who polls show tend to back Bolsonaro, older voters' support for Lula is linked to memories of improvements in living standards, including minimum wage hikes, investment in public health, and other benefits linked to Lula's earlier governments, Schulman said. "It's a memory that younger people don't have," Schulman said. Some seniors fear their benefits could diminish under a Bolsonaro government, since he is under pressure to trim Brazil's heavy public debt, and could target welfare spending. Others are concerned about what a Bolsonaro win would mean for Brazilian democracy, remembering how supporters of former President Bolsonaro attacked government buildings in January 2023 after he lost to Lula in Brazil's last election, according to research from the leftist incumbent's Workers' Party, known as PT. Near Manaus, in northern Brazil, Olga Darc Pimentel, 78, told Reuters she was deeply concerned by the runoff. "We remember the terror of the pandemic here," Pimentel said, referring to the elder Bolsonaro's widely criticized handling of the coronavirus outbreak, adding that she plans to vote for Lula and is encouraging others to do the same. Bolsonaro's campaign did not respond to requests for comment, but he can still count on plenty of elderly voters. Isaltina Rosa Peixoto, 73, a retired civil servant, said she believes Bolsonaro will continue and refresh his father's legacy. "I'm not afraid because I know he'll do what's best," she said at a pro-Bolsonaro rally in Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: UN expert urges Indonesia to reconsider involvement in Trump's Gaza board
item.description: Indonesia should reconsider its involvement in US President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan because it is being shaped by Israel and the US and lacks a Palestinian voice, the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories told Reuters on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Stanley Widianto, Gibran Peshimam
item.content:encoded: Indonesia should reconsider its involvement in US President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan because it is being shaped by Israel and the US and lacks a Palestinian voice, the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights in the occupied Palestinian territories told Reuters on Thursday. The "[USN:L6N45Q023 TEXT:"Board of Peace,"]" of which Indonesia is a key troop-contributing member, was unveiled by Trump in January to address global conflicts typically handled by the United Nations. The world's largest Muslim-majority nation has also [USN:L6N40008Q TEXT:"pledged troops"] to be deployed to Gaza as part of an international stabilisation force. Francesca Albanese, a prominent human rights lawyer known for her vocal criticism of Israel, said in an interview in Jakarta that Indonesia has historically supported the Palestinian cause, but joining the board was dangerous. Indonesia's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Board of Peace discussions remained on hold, reiterating its earlier position. Albanese has drawn the ire of a number of Western capitals. The US has imposed sanctions on her, and others, including her own native Italy, have called for her resignation. "I understand (Indonesia's) good intentions. I still think that it's very dangerous, because it risks to normalise a very abnormal mechanism," she said. Albanese said that, legally, Israel could not have a role in determining the future of Palestinians. Rights experts have criticised the board for not including a Palestinian representative even though it is meant to supervise the temporary governance of a Palestinian territory. The Board of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside US business hours. Indonesia, which backs a two-state solution and has repeatedly condemned Israeli violence, has drawn criticism from domestic Muslim groups for agreeing to join the board, which also counts Israel as a member. President Prabowo Subianto [USN:L6N3ZU1AE TEXT:"has vowed to quit"] if it does not bring benefits to Palestinians, his office has previously said, adding that joining the board would allow Indonesia to push for cessation of violence. Albanese said Indonesia risked compromising its close ties with Palestinians. "It's very risky to do so when the rules are set by Israel," she said. Albanese recommended Jakarta join the Hague Group of countries, which includes South Africa and Indonesia's neighbour Malaysia and seeks to uphold international law and processes, including in the International Criminal Court over Israel's actions. Trump's Gaza plan has stalled. [USN:L1N45F09E TEXT:"A 2025 ceasefire"] secured the release of the remaining hostages held by Hamas and hundreds of Palestinian prisoners and detainees, but efforts to disarm Hamas and secure an Israeli withdrawal have faltered, while Israeli forces continue near-daily attacks in Gaza. Israel's government has denied accusations, including by a UN commission and international and Israeli rights groups, that it is committing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

item.title: Rain delays start of final day of South Africa-Australia test
item.description: Rain delayed the start of play on the last day of the second test with South Africa needing six wickets against Australia to level the three-match series at St George’s Park on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rain delayed the start of play on the last day of the second test with South Africa needing six wickets against Australia to level the three-match series at St George’s Park on Thursday. Early lunch was taken after several abortive efforts to get play under way, leaving South Africa with only two sessions to try and force a result as Australia trail by 170 runs at 156-4 in their second innings after being forced to follow-on. Play is set to resume at noon local time (1000 GMT). Travis Head on 87 and nightwatchman Scott Boland (2) will resume the tourists' efforts at holding out while Steve Smith is available after a neck issue restricted him on Wednesday, when he batted with obvious discomfort but still top scored for Australia with 28 in their first innings of 99 and reached the milestone of 11,000 career test runs. Smith did not come out to bat in his regular No. 4 spot in the second innings, staying in the changing room receiving treatment, but on Thursday morning he warmed up with the rest of the team.

item.title: Italy, Spain lift border controls brought in after Ceuta migrant rush
item.description: Italy and Spain have agreed to lift border controls on each other's citizens, the interior ministry in Rome said on Thursday, ending a three-month dispute triggered by the rush of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy and Spain have agreed to lift [USN:L8N44S0K4 TEXT:"border controls"] on each other's citizens, the interior ministry in Rome said on Thursday, ending a three-month dispute triggered by [USN:L1N43X0ZO TEXT:"the rush of migrants"] into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Italy's right-wing government first suspended its open-border arrangements with Spain on July 31, saying it wanted to make sure no migrants entering Ceuta could travel on to its territory. Madrid responded by taking similar action against Rome, describing the Italian measures as "unjust, contrary to European Union interests, and discriminatory to the population of Spain". The Italian and Spanish interior ministers spoke on the phone and agreed not to extend their suspension of the European Union's open-border Schengen arrangements, the Italian statement said. "The decision, reached after a careful assessment of the situation, will be accompanied by enhanced information-sharing measures to ensure the full security of the common Schengen area," the ministry added. (This story has been refiled to correct the day to Thursday, from Friday, in paragraph 1.)

item.title: Fehler in Programmiersprache bringt IT-Experten um ihren Schlaf
item.description: Schwachstellen in der populären Programmiersprache PHP haben einen Wettlauf zwischen Webseitenbetreibern und Cyberkriminellen ausgelöst. Die einen arbeiteten am Donnerstag mit Hochdruck daran, eine aktualisierte Version der Software zu installieren, während die anderen die Sicherheitslücken auszunutzen versuchten. Weltweit nahmen Unternehmen, Behörden und andere Organisationen ihre Internetauftritte vorübergehend vom Netz, um ihre IT-Systeme zu schützen.
item.dc:creator: Hakan Ersen
item.content:encoded: Schwachstellen in der populären Programmiersprache PHP haben einen Wettlauf zwischen Webseitenbetreibern und Cyberkriminellen ausgelöst. Die einen arbeiteten am Donnerstag mit Hochdruck daran, eine aktualisierte Version der Software zu installieren, während die anderen die Sicherheitslücken auszunutzen versuchten. Weltweit nahmen Unternehmen, Behörden und andere Organisationen ihre Internetauftritte vorübergehend vom Netz, um ihre IT-Systeme zu schützen. Der Cybersicherheitsfirma Cloudflare (NET.N) zufolge löste das Bekanntwerden der PHP-Fehler eine Flut von Attacken aus. In den Stunden davor habe es einige tausend Versuche gegeben, die Sicherheitslücken auszunutzen, schrieb Unternehmenschef Matthew Prince auf dem Kurznachrichtendienst X. "Diese Zahl stieg in den 45 Minuten nach der Bekanntgabe auf Zehntausende, innerhalb von zwei Stunden auf Hunderttausende und geht mittlerweile in die Millionen." Die Zahl der durch die Schwachstellen potenziell gefährdeten Server und Anwendungen beziffert die Cybersicherheitsfirma Palo Alto Networks auf mehr als 22 Millionen weltweit. Schätzungen zufolge basieren etwa zwei Drittel bis drei Viertel aller Webseiten auf PHP. REGE UPDATE-TÄTIGKEIT "Die größeren Betreiber scheinen die Updates bereits eingespielt zu haben", sagte Felix Kuhlenkamp, Leiter Sicherheit beim Digitalverband Bitkom. "Nichtsdestotrotz wird uns das Thema noch lange beschäftigen. Es wird weiterhin Applikationen geben, die nicht auf dem aktuellen Stand sind. Die Frage ist dann, ob dies Konsequenzen für andere Anwendungen hat." Der deutsche Cloud-Anbieter und Webhoster Ionos (IOSn.DE) teilte am Donnerstagmorgen mit, er habe das PHP-Update bereits eingespielt. Lediglich Ionos-Kunden, die eigene Server betrieben, müssten selbst aktiv werden. Der Branchendienst Censys warnte jedoch, dass 1,5 Millionen der weltweit 2,6 Millionen Webseitenbetreiber eine veraltete PHP-Version nutzten, für die es kein Sicherheitsupdate gibt. Die PHP-Sicherheitslücke habe IT-Verantwortlichen eine schlaflose Nacht beschert, sagte Microsoft (MSFT.O) -Chef Satya Nadella auf einer Veranstaltung in Köln. "So etwas habe ich schon lange nicht mehr gesehen." Es sei ein Weckruf und erinnere die Verantwortlichen daran, dass man bei IT-Systemen nicht nur einzelne Anwendungen betrachten dürfe, sondern auch die Abhängigkeiten im Blick behalten müsse. ECKPFEILER DES WORLD WIDE WEB PHP dient als Basis für zahlreiche Webanwendungen wie Online-Shops oder Portale der öffentlichen Verwaltung. In dieser Sprache ist zudem das Softwarepaket WordPress programmiert, mit dem auch Privatpersonen Webseiten erstellen und veröffentlichen können. Die Schwachstellen seien bereits vor längerer Zeit durch Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) aufgedeckt worden, teilten zwei Cybersicherheitsfirmen unabhängig voneinander mit. Seither wurde an einer Lösung gearbeitet. Die Lücken seien mehr als ein Jahrzehnt lang unentdeckt geblieben. "Früher war das Aufspüren von Sicherheitslücken die größte Herausforderung", sagte Madeline Lawrence, Mitgründerin der Softwarefirma Aikido Security. "Die neuesten KI-Modelle machen dies sowohl für Angreifer als auch für Verteidiger wesentlich einfacher. Es erfordert weniger Zeit, Geld und Fachwissen, um eine Schwachstelle für einen Angriff zu nutzen." Dadurch werde es immer schwieriger, rasch Gegenmaßnahmen zu ergreifen. Die Entwickler von PHP hatten am Mittwochnachmittag (MESZ) eine aktualisierte Version (PHP 8.5.12) veröffentlicht und eindringlich dazu geraten, diese umgehend zu installieren. Das Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik (BSI) schloss sich dieser Aufforderung ebenso an wie das chinesische Industrieministerium. Die südkoreanische Regierung ergriff Notfallmaßnahmen.

item.title: France reports first human case of livestock virus Shamonda
item.description: France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage.
item.dc:creator: Sybille de La Hamaide
item.content:encoded: France on Thursday reported the first human case of the Shamonda virus usually found in livestock in a patient who later died, with authorities adding there was no risk to the general population at this stage. Transmitted by biting midges and most commonly found in cattle, Shamonda has also been found in horses, alpaca, sheep and goats, the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) said. "The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control is carefully monitoring the situation after the French authorities announced the first ever reported human infection with Shamonda virus, a disease that has until now only affected animals," the Stockholm-based ECDC said in a statement. "ECDC is in contact with the French authorities and European partners to investigate the potential public health implications." The French announcement said the leading hypothesis was that the patient was infected in eastern France, where the virus had circulated among animals this spring and summer. "Based on the knowledge available regarding this virus, no health risk to the general population has been identified to date," it said. The ECDC said the patient died in early October and noted the victim had been receiving treatment for a serious illness that made them more susceptible to infection than the general population. "Investigations into whether the virus caused or contributed to the patient’s death and how the infection was acquired are ongoing," it said. There are currently no commercially available vaccines against Shamonda virus, WOAH said. Identified in Nigeria in the mid-1960s, Shamonda was first confirmed in Europe in late July after genomic tests on sick cattle in southern Germany, Switzerland and eastern France. A report from France's weekly animal health surveillance bulletin said the virus had also been detected in Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, and UK's Jersey. A study of French nine dairy farms found milk output fell by up to 75% in affected herds.

item.title: TSMC seeks factory-equipment alternatives to thwart China's rare earths grip, sources say
item.description: Taiwan's TSMC is exploring alternatives to rare-earth components in factory equipment, three people familiar with the matter said, aiming to reduce the risk that Beijing's export controls could disrupt operations at plants that make the world's most advanced chips.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yee Lee, Fanny Potkin
item.content:encoded: Taiwan's TSMC (2330.TW) is exploring alternatives to rare-earth components in factory equipment, three people familiar with the matter said, aiming to reduce the risk that Beijing's export controls could disrupt operations at plants that make the world's most advanced chips. The move, reported for the first time, underscores how China's grip on rare earths has become a vulnerability for the global semiconductor industry after the country last year put certain rare-earth materials, magnets and related processing technology under export controls, requiring licences. Rare-earth magnets are commonly used in motors that power moving parts in industrial equipment, including machinery found in highly automated factories such as those operated by TSMC. A shortage of such specialised parts could disrupt chip production for customers in smartphone, AI system, data centre and defence supply chains. TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, has surveyed suppliers on using rare-earth-free motors in factory-automation equipment, according to three industry executives briefed by the company on its plans. One of the people said the effort was driven by concerns about potential supply disruptions from China. The discussions remain at an early stage and have not yet resulted in a broad rollout of rare-earth-free equipment, according to two of the people. TSMC declined to comment. WASHINGTON AND TAIPEI SEEK ALTERNATIVES TSMC's efforts follow statements from the United States and Taiwan that they would begin looking for ways to reduce their reliance on Chinese rare-earth and critical-mineral supply chains. In June, Raymond F. Greene, the director of the American Institute in Taiwan, Washington's de facto embassy in Taipei, said the United States is working with Taiwan and other partners to develop alternative sources of supply, expand processing capacity and build more resilient supply chains. Taiwan's Economy Minister Kung Ming-hsin said in February that the government would give support to the Industrial Technology Research Institute (ITRI), a domestic research organisation, to develop rare-earth technologies, with plans to establish a pilot production line within three years that could meet an estimated 50% of the island's domestic demand. US officials have shown particular interest in ITRI's work and have engaged the institute in talks about diversifying critical-mineral supply chains, according to a person at a US-based think tank familiar with the discussions. The US State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In a statement, ITRI said it was working with the Department of Industrial Technology at Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs to plan a rare-earth project. It did not provide further comment.

item.title: Four people die as storms, flooding hit southern France
item.description: At least four people have died in storms and flooding in southern France, authorities said late on Wednesday, as western regions braced for another storm approaching from Ireland.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least four people have died in storms and flooding in southern France, authorities said late on Wednesday, as western regions braced for another storm approaching from Ireland. Dozens of people moved to emergency shelters in Mouries and Saint-Martin-de-Crau — two small towns between Montpellier and Marseille — and at least one person was injured, officials said Roads and train lines in the area were disrupted, Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot wrote in a post on X Forecasters said the weather would settle down in the south But Storm Austen was expected to bring heavy winds across the northwest later on Thursday into Friday, weather agency Meteo France said
